title.raw: 卷三百五十五 列傳第一百十四 賈易 董敦逸 上官均 來之邵 葉濤 楊畏 崔台符 楊汲 呂嘉問 李南公 董必 虞策 郭知章 Volume 355 Biographies 114: Jia Yi, Dong Dunyi, Shang Guanjun, Lai ZhiShao, Ye Tao, Yang Wei, Cui Taifu, Yang Ji, Lu Jiawen, Li Nangong, Dong Bi, Yu Ce, Guo Zhizhang

sentences.zh: 賈易，字明叔，無為人。

translations.literal: Jia Yi, styled Mingshu, was a native of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi, courtesy name Mingshu, came from Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 七歲而孤。

translations.literal: At seven he was orphaned.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father when he was seven.

sentences.zh: 母彭，以紡績自給，日與易十錢，使從學。

translations.literal: His mother Peng supported herself by spinning and weaving, giving Yi ten cash each day so he could study.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Peng earned their living by spinning and weaving, giving Yi ten copper cash a day for his schooling.

sentences.zh: 易不忍使一錢，每浹旬，輒復歸之。

translations.literal: Yi could not bear to spend a single cash; every ten days he would return them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi hated to spend even one coin; every ten days or so he would bring the money back to her.

sentences.zh: 年逾冠，中進士甲科，調常州司法參軍。

translations.literal: After coming of age he passed the jinshi in the top class and was appointed judicial adjutant in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After he came of age, he placed in the top tier of the jinshi examination and was appointed judicial adjutant in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 自以儒者不閑法令，歲議獄，唯求合於人情，曰：「人情所在，法亦在焉。

translations.literal: Considering himself a Confucian scholar unfamiliar with statutes, when he reviewed cases each year he sought only what accorded with human feeling, saying: "Where human feeling lies, the law lies there too.
translations.idiomatic: He regarded himself as a scholar of the classics, not versed in penal law; when he heard cases each year he looked only for what matched common human feeling, saying, "Where human feeling is, the law is as well.

sentences.zh: 」訖去，郡中稱平。

translations.literal: " When he left at the end of his term, the prefecture called his judgments fair.
translations.idiomatic: " By the time he left office, the prefecture praised his judgments as even-handed.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，為太常丞、兵部員外郎，遷左司諫。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanyou era he served as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Vice Minister of War, then was transferred to Left Remonstrance Bureau censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanyou reign he held the posts of Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Vice Minister of War, then was promoted to censor in the Left Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 論呂陶不爭張舜民事，與陶交攻，遂劾陶黨附蘇軾兄弟，並及文彥博、范純仁。

translations.literal: He criticized Lü Tao for not contesting Zhang Shunmin's case, clashed with Tao in mutual attacks, and memorialized that Tao was partisan with Su Shi and his brother, also implicating Wen Yanbo and Fan Chunren.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Lü Tao for failing to dispute the Zhang Shunmin affair, traded blows with Tao in memorials, and then impeached Tao as allied with Su Shi and his brother, extending the charge to Wen Yanbo and Fan Chunren.

sentences.zh: 宣仁后怒其訐，欲謫之，呂公著救之力，出知懷州。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren was angered by his calumny and wished to demote him; Lü Gongzhu strongly intervened, and he was sent out as prefect of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren was furious at his slander and wanted him banished; Lü Gongzhu argued strenuously on his behalf, and he was instead appointed prefect of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 御史言其謝表文過，徙廣德軍。

translations.literal: A censor said his memorial of thanks was excessive in wording, and he was transferred to Guangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: A supervising censor complained that his letter of thanks was immoderate in tone, and he was reassigned to Guangde Army.

sentences.zh: 明年，提點江東刑獄，召拜殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: The next year he was made judicial intendant for Jiangdong and summoned as Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed judicial intendant for Jiangdong, then recalled and named Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 遂疏彥博至和建儲之議為不然，宣仁后命付史館，彥博不自安，竟解平章重事而去。

translations.literal: He then memorialized that Yanbo's Zhihe proposal to establish an heir was wrong; Empress Dowager Xuanren ordered it filed in the Historiography Office; Yanbo felt uneasy and finally resigned his post as Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial disputing Yanbo's Zhihe plan for establishing an heir; Empress Dowager Xuanren ordered the document placed in the Historiography Office; Yanbo grew uneasy and in the end relinquished his grand councillor post.

sentences.zh: 蘇轍為中丞，易引前嫌求避，改度支員外郎，孫升以為左遷。

translations.literal: When Su Zhe became chief censor, Yi cited old grievances and asked to be excused, and was changed to Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau; Sun Sheng regarded this as a demotion.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Zhe became chief censor, Yi pleaded prior animosity and asked to step aside; he was reassigned as Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau, which Sun Sheng took to be a demotion.

sentences.zh: 又改國子司業，不拜，提點淮東刑獄。

translations.literal: He was again changed to Vice Director of the Imperial University but did not accept the appointment, and was made judicial intendant for Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: He was next named Vice Director of the Imperial University but declined the post, and was appointed judicial intendant for Huaidong.

sentences.zh: 復入，為侍御史。

translations.literal: He returned to the capital and served as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court and made Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 上書言：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne, saying:

sentences.zh: 「天下大勢可畏者五：一曰上下相蒙，而毀譽不得其真。

translations.literal: "Five things in the great trend of the realm are to be feared: first, superiors and inferiors deceive one another, so praise and blame do not obtain their truth.
translations.idiomatic: "There are five trends in the empire that ought to alarm us. The first is that superiors and subordinates deceive one another, so that praise and blame no longer reflect reality.

sentences.zh: 故人主聰明壅蔽，下情不得上達；

translations.literal: Thus the ruler's intelligence is blocked and obscured, and conditions below cannot reach above;
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's clear sight is blocked, and what happens below never reaches the throne;

sentences.zh: 邪正無別，而君子之道日消，小人之黨日進。

translations.literal: the wicked and the upright are not distinguished, the way of the gentleman daily wanes, and the faction of petty men daily advances.
translations.idiomatic: wrong and right are no longer distinguished, the way of the gentleman dwindles day by day, and the cliques of petty men advance.

sentences.zh: 二曰政事苟且，而官人不任其責。

translations.literal: Second, government affairs are perfunctory, and officials do not bear their responsibilities.
translations.idiomatic: Second, public business is handled in a slipshod way, and officials do not shoulder their duties.

sentences.zh: 故治道不成，萬事隳廢，惡吏市姦而自得，良民受弊而無告；

translations.literal: Thus the way of governance is not achieved, the myriad affairs are ruined and abandoned, wicked clerks trade in villainy to their own profit, and good people suffer harm with none to whom they can appeal;
translations.idiomatic: As a result good government never takes shape, every undertaking decays, corrupt clerks peddle fraud for their own gain, and honest people suffer injury with nowhere to turn;

sentences.zh: 愁歎不平之氣，充溢宇宙，以干陰陽之和。

translations.literal: the air of grief, sighing, and injustice fills heaven and earth, disturbing the harmony of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: grief, resentment, and injustice fill the world and disturb the harmony of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 三曰經費不充，而生財不得其道。

translations.literal: Third, revenue is insufficient, and the generation of wealth does not follow the right path.
translations.idiomatic: Third, state funds are inadequate because wealth is not being created by proper means.

sentences.zh: 故公私困弊，無及時預備之計，衣食之源日蹙；

translations.literal: Thus public and private are exhausted and distressed, there is no timely plan for provision, and the sources of food and clothing daily grow tight;
translations.idiomatic: Public and private resources alike are strained, there is no timely plan of reserve, and the sources of food and clothing shrink daily;

sentences.zh: 無事之時尚猶有患，不幸倉卒多事，則狼狽窮迫而禍敗至矣。

translations.literal: even in times without trouble there is still worry; if by misfortune sudden crises multiply, then in panic and extremity disaster and defeat will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: even in quiet times trouble already looms; should sudden crises pile up, the state will be driven to desperation and ruin.

sentences.zh: 四曰人材廢闕，而教養不以其方。

translations.literal: Fourth, human talent is wasted and lacking, and nurture and instruction do not follow the proper method.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, talent is neglected and training does not follow the right path.

sentences.zh: 故士君子無可用之實，而愚不肖充牣於朝；

translations.literal: Thus gentlemen have no practical ability to be employed, while the foolish and unworthy fill the court;
translations.idiomatic: Men of worth have no real use to offer, while the foolish and incompetent crowd the court;

sentences.zh: 汙合苟容之俗滋長，背上欺君之風益扇，士氣浸弱，將誰與立太平之基。

translations.literal: the custom of filthy compromise and easy tolerance grows, the wind of turning one's back to deceive the ruler fans ever stronger, the spirit of scholars weakens by degrees—with whom will the foundation of great peace be laid?
translations.idiomatic: the habit of filthy compromise spreads, the fashion of deceiving the ruler from behind grows stronger, and the morale of scholars weakens—who then will help lay the foundations of lasting peace?

sentences.zh: 五曰刑賞失中，而人心不知所向。

translations.literal: Fifth, punishments and rewards miss the mean, and people's hearts do not know where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, rewards and punishments are misapplied, and the people no longer know what to aim for.

sentences.zh: 故以非為是，以黑為白，更相欺惑，以罔其上；

translations.literal: Thus wrong is taken for right, black for white; they deceive and bewilder one another to mislead their superiors;
translations.idiomatic: Wrong is treated as right and black as white; men deceive one another to mislead their superiors;

sentences.zh: 爵之以高祿而不加勸，僇之以顯罰而不加懼，徼利苟免之姦，冒貨犯義之俗，將何所不有。

translations.literal: ennobling with high salary does not add encouragement, punishing with conspicuous penalty does not add fear—what will not exist among the villainy of grasping profit and seeking easy escape, and the custom of coveting goods and violating righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: high office no longer encourages virtue, nor do severe punishments inspire fear—every sort of scheming for profit and evasion of duty, every custom of greed and breach of righteousness, will flourish unchecked.

sentences.zh: 今二聖焦勞念治，而天下之勢乃如此，任事者不可以不憂。

translations.literal: Now the Two Sages toil with care for good governance, yet the trend of the realm is thus—those who bear office cannot fail to be concerned.
translations.idiomatic: The Two Sovereigns labor tirelessly for good government, yet the empire stands in this condition; those who hold office cannot afford to be indifferent.

sentences.zh: 是猶寢於積薪之上，火未及然，而自以為安，可不畏乎？

translations.literal: This is like sleeping on a pile of kindling—the fire has not yet caught, yet one thinks oneself safe; can one fail to be afraid?
translations.idiomatic: It is as though one slept on a heap of firewood: the flames have not yet caught, yet one imagines oneself safe—should that not terrify us?

sentences.zh: 然則欲知毀譽真偽之情，則莫若明目達聰，使下無壅蔽之患。

translations.literal: If one wishes to know the truth and falsity of praise and blame, there is nothing like clear sight and penetrating hearing, so that below there is no affliction of blockage and concealment.
translations.idiomatic: If we wish to know whether praise and blame are true, nothing is better than to open our eyes and ears so that nothing below is blocked from view.

sentences.zh: 欲官人皆任其責，則莫若詢事考言，循名責實。

translations.literal: If one wishes all officials to bear their responsibilities, there is nothing like inquiring into affairs and examining words, following names to demand realities.
translations.idiomatic: If we wish every official to shoulder his duty, we should examine deeds and test words, holding men to the titles they bear.

sentences.zh: 欲生財不逆其道，則莫若敦本業而抑末作，崇儉約而戒奢僭。

translations.literal: If one wishes wealth to be generated without violating the Way, there is nothing like honoring the fundamental occupations and restraining secondary crafts, exalting frugality and warning against luxury and presumption.
translations.idiomatic: If we wish wealth to be created in the right way, we should encourage the root occupations and restrain secondary trades, honor frugality, and warn against extravagance and presumption.

sentences.zh: 欲教養必以其方，則莫若廣詳延之路，厲廉恥之節，使公卿大臣各舉所知，召對延問，以觀其能否，善者用之，不善者罷之。

translations.literal: If one wishes nurture and instruction necessarily to follow the proper method, there is nothing like broadening paths of detailed recommendation, strengthening the integrity of integrity and shame, causing grandees and ministers each to recommend those they know, summoning them for audience and prolonged questioning to observe their ability—the capable are employed, the incapable dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: If training is to follow the right method, we should widen avenues of recommendation, strengthen standards of integrity and shame, have ministers recommend men they know, summon them for audience and questioning to test their ability, employ the able, and dismiss the unfit.

sentences.zh: 欲人心皆知所向，則莫若賞以勸善，刑以懲惡，不以親疏貴賤為之輕重。

translations.literal: If one wishes all hearts to know where to turn, there is nothing like rewarding to encourage good and punishing to chastise evil, not making light or heavy according to closeness, distance, nobility, or baseness.
translations.idiomatic: If the people's hearts are to know their direction, we should reward to encourage good and punish to restrain evil, without regard to kinship, distance, rank, or low birth.

sentences.zh: 則民志一定，而放僻邪侈不為矣。」

translations.literal: Then the people's will is fixed, and depravity, perversity, evil, and excess will not be done."
translations.idiomatic: Then the people's purpose will be settled, and depravity and excess will cease."

sentences.zh: 其言雖頗切直，然皆老生常談，志於抵阨時事，無他奇畫。

translations.literal: Though his words were rather blunt and direct, they were all stale commonplaces; his aim was to obstruct current affairs, with no other remarkable plan.
translations.idiomatic: His language was blunt enough, but it was all familiar platitudes; he meant only to obstruct the times, and offered nothing original.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾守杭，訴浙西災潦甚苦。

translations.literal: Su Shi was prefect of Hangzhou and reported that the flood disaster in western Zhejiang was extremely severe.
translations.idiomatic: While Su Shi was prefect of Hangzhou, he reported that western Zhejiang had suffered grievously from flood and drought.

sentences.zh: 易率其僚楊畏、安鼎論軾姑息邀譽，眩惑朝聽，乞加考實。

translations.literal: Yi led his colleagues Yang Wei and An Ding in memorializing that Shi was indulgent and sought reputation, bewildering the court's hearing, and begged that investigation be added.
translations.idiomatic: Yi joined his colleagues Yang Wei and An Ding in charging that Shi was coddling the people to win praise and misleading the court, and asked that the matter be investigated.

sentences.zh: 詔下，給事中范祖禹封還之，以謂正宜闊略不問，以活百姓。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Supervising Secretary Fan Zuyu sealed and returned it, saying that one should rightly be broad and lenient without inquiry, to keep the people alive.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict went out, Supervising Secretary Fan Zuyu returned it sealed, arguing that the court ought rather to overlook the matter and let the people live.

sentences.zh: 易遂言：「軾頃在揚州題詩，以奉先帝遺詔為『聞好語』；

translations.literal: Yi then said: "Shi recently composed a poem in Yangzhou, treating the late emperor's testamentary edict as 'hearing fine words';
translations.idiomatic: Yi then memorialized: "Shi lately wrote a poem in Yangzhou in which he treated the late emperor's testamentary edict as merely 'hearing fine words';

sentences.zh: 草呂大防制云『民亦勞止』，引周厲王詩以比熙寧、元豐之政。

translations.literal: drafting Lü Dafang's appointment text with 'the people also are weary and halt,' citing the Zhou poem on King Li to compare with the policies of Xining and Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: in drafting Lü Dafang's appointment edict he wrote 'the people too are weary and halt,' citing the ode on King Li of Zhou to liken the Xining and Yuanfeng policies to tyranny.

sentences.zh: 弟轍蚤應制科試，文繆不應格，幸而濫進，與軾昔皆誹怨先帝，無人臣禮。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhe early took the special examination; his essay was erroneous and did not meet the standard, yet by fortune he was rashly advanced; like Shi in the past, both slandered and resented the late emperor, without the rites of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhe took the special examination early; his essay was flawed and should have failed, yet he was improperly advanced; both brothers have long slandered the late emperor and shown themselves unworthy of a subject's duty.

sentences.zh: 」至指李林甫、楊國忠為喻，議者由是薄易，出知宣州。

translations.literal: " He even cited Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong as analogies; discussers therefore looked down on Yi, and he was sent out as prefect of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He even compared them to Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong; critics despised him for it, and he was appointed prefect of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 除京西轉運副使，徙蘇州、徐州，加直秘閣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Transport Commissioner for Jingxi, transferred to Suzhou and Xuzhou, and given the honorary title Direct Access to the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Transport Commissioner for the Jingxi circuit, then served in Suzhou and Xuzhou, and was granted the honorary title Direct Access to the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 元符中，累謫保靜軍行軍司馬，邵州安置。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfu era he was repeatedly demoted to Acting Military Affairs Officer of Baojing Army and settled in Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfu reign he was repeatedly demoted to Acting Military Affairs Officer of Baojing Army and exiled to Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，召為太常少卿，進右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and advanced to Right Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong came to the throne, Yi was recalled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to Right Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 陳次升論其為曾布客，改權刑部侍郎，歷工部、吏部，未滿歲為真。

translations.literal: Chen Cisheng argued that he was a client of Zeng Bu; he was changed to Acting Vice Minister of Justice, passed through the Ministries of Works and Personnel, and before a year had passed received the substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Cisheng charged that he was a follower of Zeng Bu; he was reassigned as Acting Vice Minister of Justice, then served in the Ministries of Works and Personnel, and within a year received the substantive post.

sentences.zh: 以寶文閣待制知鄧州，尋入黨籍。

translations.literal: As Academician-Awaiting Orders of the Baowen Pavilion he was prefect of Dengzhou; soon he was entered on the faction register.
translations.idiomatic: As Academician-Awaiting Orders of the Baowen Pavilion he governed Dengzhou; soon afterward he was listed among the proscribed faction.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 董敦逸

translations.literal: Dong Dunyi
translations.idiomatic: Dong Dunyi

sentences.zh: 董敦逸，字夢授，吉州永豐人。

translations.literal: Dong Dunyi, styled Mengshou, was a native of Yongfeng in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Dunyi, courtesy name Mengshou, came from Yongfeng in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，調連州司理參軍、知穰縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed judicial adjutant in Lianzhou and magistrate of Rang County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed judicial adjutant in Lianzhou and magistrate of Rang County.

sentences.zh: 時方興水利，提舉官調民鑿馬渡港，雲可灌田二百頃，敦逸言於朝，以為利不補害，核實如敦逸言。

translations.literal: At the time water conservancy was being promoted; the supervising official mobilized the people to dig the Madu Harbor, saying it could irrigate two hundred qing of fields; Dunyi spoke to the court that the benefit would not repay the harm, and verification was as Dunyi said.
translations.idiomatic: When waterworks were being pushed forward, a supervising official conscripted labor to dig Madu Harbor, claiming it would irrigate two hundred qing of fields; Dunyi reported to court that the gain would not repay the cost, and investigation proved him right.

sentences.zh: 免役夫十六萬，全舊田三千六百頃。

translations.literal: One hundred sixty thousand corvée laborers were spared, and three thousand six hundred qing of existing fields were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred sixty thousand corvée laborers were spared, and three thousand six hundred qing of existing farmland were preserved.

sentences.zh: 徙知弋陽縣，寶豐銅冶役卒多困於誘略，有致死者，敦逸推見本末，縱還鄉者數百人。

translations.literal: Transferred as magistrate of Yiyang County; at Baofeng copper smelting many conscript laborers suffered from enticement and coercion, and some died; Dunyi traced matters to their roots and released several hundred to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Yiyang County; at the Baofeng copper works many conscript laborers had been trapped by coercion, and some died; Dunyi traced the affair to its source and sent several hundred men home.

sentences.zh: 稍遷梓州路轉運判官。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Transport Assessor of Zizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Transport Assessor of Zizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 元祐六年，召為監察御史，同御史黃慶基言：「蘇軾昔為中書舍人，制誥中指斥先帝事，其弟轍相為表裏，以紊朝政。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanyou he was summoned as Supervising Censor; together with Censor Huang Qingji he said: "Su Shi formerly as Secretariat Drafter in his edicts pointed and reproached matters of the late emperor; his younger brother Zhe acted as inner and outer with him to disorder court governance."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanyou he was summoned as Supervising Censor; together with Censor Huang Qingji he charged: "When Su Shi served as Secretariat Drafter, his edicts criticized the late emperor; his brother Zhe worked hand in glove with him to throw court affairs into confusion."

sentences.zh: 」宰相呂大防奏曰：「敦逸、慶基言軾所撰制詞，以為謗毀先帝。

translations.literal: " Grand Councillor Lü Dafang memorialized: "Dunyi and Qingji speak of the edict text Shi drafted, taking it as slandering the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Councillor Lü Dafang replied: "Dunyi and Qingji claim that the edict Shi drafted slanders the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀先帝聖意，本欲富國強兵，鞭撻不庭，一時群臣將順太過，故事或失當。

translations.literal: Your servant privately observes the late emperor's sagely intent was originally to enrich the state and strengthen the army, to whip those who would not come to court; for a time the ministers followed and yielded excessively, and some measures were perhaps inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the late emperor's true aim was to enrich the state and strengthen the army and to chastise those who would not submit; for a time the ministers flattered him too readily, and some measures went awry.

sentences.zh: 及太皇太后與皇帝臨御，因民所欲，隨事救改，蓋事理當然爾。

translations.literal: When the Grand Empress Dowager and the emperor took the throne, following what the people desired, they amended matters as needed—this is surely how principle and circumstance naturally are.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Empress Dowager and the emperor took power, they amended policies according to the people's wishes—this was only what reason required.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝好用兵，重斂傷民，昭帝嗣位，博采眾議，多行寢罷，明帝尚察，屢興慘獄，章帝改之以寬厚，天下悅服，未有以為謗毀先帝者也。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han loved using troops and heavy levies that harmed the people; when Emperor Zhao succeeded, he broadly gathered many opinions and largely suspended and abolished them; Emperor Ming valued scrutiny and repeatedly raised cruel prisons; Emperor Zhang changed this with lenience and generosity, and the realm was pleased and submitted—none took this as slandering the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han loved war and heavy taxation that harmed the people; when Emperor Zhao succeeded, he gathered counsel widely and repealed many measures; Emperor Ming was severe and raised cruel prosecutions; Emperor Zhang replaced severity with lenience, and the realm rejoiced—no one called that slandering the former emperor.

sentences.zh: 至如本朝真宗即位，弛放逋欠以厚民財；

translations.literal: As for our dynasty, when Emperor Zhenzong ascended he relaxed and released arrears to enrich the people's wealth;
translations.idiomatic: In our own dynasty, when Zhenzong came to the throne he remitted tax arrears to ease the people's burden;

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，罷修宮觀以息民力。

translations.literal: when Emperor Renzong ascended he halted the repair of palaces and temples to rest the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: when Renzong came to the throne he halted palace and temple construction to spare the people's labor.

sentences.zh: 凡此皆因時施宜，以補助先朝闕政，亦未聞當時士大夫有以為謗毀先帝者也。

translations.literal: All these followed the times and applied what was fitting, to supplement and aid the previous court's deficient policies; nor has one heard that the scholar-officials of the time took this as slandering the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: All of this was timely adjustment to remedy the previous reign's shortcomings; no scholar-official of those days called it slander of the former emperor.

sentences.zh: 比惟元祐以來，言事官用此以中傷士人，兼欲動搖朝廷，意極不善。

translations.literal: Recently since Yuanyou, remonstrating officials have used this to strike at scholars, and moreover wish to shake the court—the intent is extremely ill.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuanyou, remonstrating officials have used this charge to wound worthy men and even to shake the court—an intent that is wholly malign.

sentences.zh: 」轍復奏曰：「臣昨日取兄軾所撰呂惠卿告觀之，其言及先帝者，有曰：『始以帝堯之仁，姑試伯鯀；

translations.literal: " Zhe again memorialized: "Your servant yesterday took my elder brother Shi's drafted dismissal notice for Lü Huiqing and examined it; where it speaks of the late emperor, there is: 'At first with Emperor Yao's benevolence, for a time he tried Gun;
translations.idiomatic: " Su Zhe replied: "Yesterday I examined the dismissal notice my brother Shi drafted for Lü Huiqing; where it mentions the late emperor, it says, 'At first, with the benevolence of Emperor Yao, he tried Gun for a time;

sentences.zh: 終然孔子之聖，不信宰予。

translations.literal: in the end with Confucius's sageliness, he did not trust Zai Yu.'
translations.idiomatic: in the end, with the sagacity of Confucius, he would not trust Zai Yu.'

sentences.zh: 』兄軾亦豈是謗毀先帝者邪？

translations.literal: ' Is my elder brother Shi one who slanders the late emperor?
translations.idiomatic: ' How can my brother Shi be called a slanderer of the late emperor?

sentences.zh: 臣聞先帝末年，亦自深悔已行之事，但未暇改爾。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in his last years the late emperor himself deeply regretted what had already been done, but had not yet had leisure to change it.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in his last years the late emperor deeply regretted what he had already done, but had not yet had time to change course.

sentences.zh: 元祐改更，蓋追述先帝美意而已。

translations.literal: The Yuanyou revisions were merely following up and recounting the late emperor's fine intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanyou reforms merely carried out the late emperor's own better intentions.

sentences.zh: 」宣仁后曰：「先帝追悔往事，至於泣下。

translations.literal: " Empress Dowager Xuanren said: "The late emperor repented past affairs, even to the point of weeping.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Dowager Xuanren said: "The late emperor repented what had been done, even to the point of tears.

sentences.zh: 」大防曰：「先帝一時過舉，非其本意。

translations.literal: " Dafang said: "The late emperor's measures for a time were excessive; they were not his original intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Dafang said: "The late emperor's excesses were momentary; they were not his true intent.

sentences.zh: 」宣仁后曰：「皇帝宜深知。

translations.literal: " Empress Dowager Xuanren said: "The emperor should deeply understand this.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Dowager Xuanren said: "Your Majesty should understand this deeply.

sentences.zh: 」於是敦逸、慶基並罷。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Dunyi and Qingji were both dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Dunyi and Qingji were both dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 敦逸出為湖北運判，改知臨江軍。

translations.literal: Dunyi went out as Transport Assessor for Hubei and was changed to prefect of Linjiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Dunyi was sent out as Transport Assessor for Hubei, then appointed prefect of Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，軾、轍失位，劉拯訟敦逸無罪。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng, when Shi and Zhe lost their posts, Liu Cheng pleaded that Dunyi was innocent.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shaosheng reign, when the Su brothers fell from power, Liu Cheng argued that Dunyi had done no wrong.

sentences.zh: 哲宗記其人，曰：「非前日白鬚御史乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong remembered the man and said: "Is this not the white-bearded censor of the other day?
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong remembered him and said, "Is this not the white-bearded censor from before?

sentences.zh: 」復除監察御史。

translations.literal: " He was again appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: " He was again appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 論常安民為二蘇之黨，凡論議主元祐者，斥去之。

translations.literal: He argued that Chang Anmin was of the Two Su faction; all whose discourse favored Yuanyou were driven out.
translations.idiomatic: He charged that Chang Anmin belonged to the Su faction; all who upheld Yuanyou policies in debate were removed.

sentences.zh: 改工部員外郎，遷殿中待御史、左司諫、侍御史，入謝曰：「臣再汙言路，第恐擠逐，不能久奉彈糾之責。

translations.literal: Changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, promoted to Palace Attendant Censor, Left Remonstrance Bureau censor, and Attending Censor; on entering to give thanks he said: "Your servant again stains the path of speech; I only fear being crowded out and cannot long fulfill the duty of impeachment and correction.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, then promoted through Palace Attendant Censor, Left Remonstrance Bureau censor, and Attending Censor; on presenting thanks he said, "I have again been granted the path of remonstrance, but I fear being driven out and cannot long fulfill the duty of impeachment.

sentences.zh: 」哲宗曰：「卿能言，無患朕之不能聽；

translations.literal: " Zhezong said: "You can speak; do not worry that We cannot listen;
translations.idiomatic: " Zhezong said, "If you can speak, do not fear that I will not listen;

sentences.zh: 卿言而信，無患朕之不能行也。」

translations.literal: if what you say is trusted, do not worry that We cannot act."
translations.idiomatic: if what you say is true, do not fear that I will not act on it."

sentences.zh: 瑤華秘獄成，詔詣掖庭錄問。

translations.literal: When the secret case of Yaohua was completed, an edict ordered him to go to the Inner Palace to record and question.
translations.idiomatic: When the secret investigation of Princess Yaohua was concluded, an edict ordered him to go to the Inner Palace to record the interrogation.

sentences.zh: 敦逸察知冤狀，握筆弗忍書，郝隨從旁脅之，乃不敢異。

translations.literal: Dunyi perceived the wrongful circumstances, held the brush and could not bear to write; Hao Sui from the side coerced him, and he dared not differ.
translations.idiomatic: Dunyi saw that the case was unjust, but could not bring himself to write; Hao Sui stood beside him and threatened him, so he dared not dissent.

sentences.zh: 獄既上，於心終不安。

translations.literal: After the case was submitted, in his heart he was never at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After the record was submitted, his conscience would not rest.

sentences.zh: 幾兩旬，竟上疏，其略云：「瑤華之廢，事有所因，情有可察。

translations.literal: After nearly twenty days he finally submitted a memorial; its gist said: "The deposing of Yaohua had its causes in the affair, and feeling can be discerned.
translations.idiomatic: After nearly twenty days he finally memorialized the throne, writing in part: "The deposition of Princess Yaohua had its causes, and the circumstances deserve scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 詔下之日，天為之陰翳，是天不欲廢之也；

translations.literal: On the day the edict was issued, heaven made it overcast—this is heaven not wishing her deposed;
translations.idiomatic: On the day the edict was issued, the sky darkened—Heaven did not wish her deposed;

sentences.zh: 人為之流涕，是人不欲廢之也。

translations.literal: people wept for her—this is the people not wishing her deposed.
translations.idiomatic: the people wept—mankind did not wish her deposed.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗閱錄其獄，恐得罪天下。

translations.literal: Your servant once reviewed and recorded her case, fearing to offend all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When I recorded her case, I feared offending all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」哲宗讀之怒，蔡卞欲加重貶，章惇、曾布以為不可，曰：「陛下本以皇城獄出於近習，故使臺端錄問，冀以取信中外。

translations.literal: " Zhezong read it in anger; Cai Bian wished to add heavier demotion; Zhang Dun and Zeng Bu thought this could not be done, saying: "Your Majesty originally because the Inner City case came from close attendants, therefore had the censorate record and question, hoping thereby to gain trust within and without.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhezong read it in anger; Cai Bian wanted a heavier punishment; Zhang Dun and Zeng Bu objected, saying, "Your Majesty originally had the censorate record the case because the Inner City investigation came from close attendants, hoping thereby to win trust at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 今謫敦逸，何以解天下後世之謗。

translations.literal: Now if Dunyi is demoted, how can the slander of all under heaven and later ages be answered?
translations.idiomatic: If Dunyi is now banished, how will Your Majesty answer the reproach of the world and of posterity?

sentences.zh: 」哲宗意解而止。

translations.literal: " Zhezong's mind was eased and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhezong's anger eased and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 明年，用他事出知興國軍，徙江州。

translations.literal: The next year, on another matter he was sent out as prefect of Xingguo Army and transferred to Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, on another charge he was sent out as prefect of Xingguo and then transferred to Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 上官均

translations.literal: Shang Guanjun
translations.idiomatic: Shang Guanjun

sentences.zh: 上官均，字彥衡，邵武人。

translations.literal: Shang Guanjun, styled Yanheng, was a native of Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Guanjun, courtesy name Yanheng, came from Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧親策進士，擢第二，為北京留守推官、國子直講。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shenzong's Xining personally examined jinshi, he was raised to second place and made judicial adjutant to the Beijing garrison commander and Lecturer in the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xining palace examination of Emperor Shenzong, he placed second and was appointed judicial adjutant to the Beijing garrison commander and Lecturer in the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，蔡確薦為監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng era Cai Que recommended him as Acting Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng reign Cai Que recommended him for appointment as Acting Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 時相州富人子殺人，讞獄為審刑、大理所疑，京師流言法官竇莘等受賕。

translations.literal: At the time a rich man's son in Xiangzhou committed murder; the case report was doubted by the Court of Judicial Review and the Court of Imperial Appeals, and in the capital rumors spread that the judges Dou Shen and others had taken bribes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a wealthy man's son in Xiangzhou committed murder; the Court of Judicial Review and the Court of Imperial Appeals questioned the verdict, and rumor spread in the capital that the judges Dou Shen and others had taken bribes.

sentences.zh: 蔡確引猜險吏數十人，窮治莘等慘酷，無敢明其冤。

translations.literal: Cai Que brought in several dozen suspicious and ruthless clerks, exhaustively prosecuting Shen and others with cruel severity; none dared declare their innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que brought in dozens of suspicious and ruthless clerks and prosecuted Shen and others with extreme cruelty; no one dared speak up for their innocence.

sentences.zh: 均上疏言之，乞以獄事詔臣參治，坐是，謫知光澤縣。

translations.literal: Jun memorialized on this, begging that the case be ordered for his participation in the investigation; for this he was demoted to magistrate of Guangze County.
translations.idiomatic: Jun memorialized on the affair and asked to be ordered to join the investigation; for this he was demoted to magistrate of Guangze County.

sentences.zh: 莘等卒無罪，天下服其持平。

translations.literal: Shen and the others in the end were without guilt; all under heaven admired his even-handedness.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and the others were ultimately found innocent, and the realm admired Jun's fairness.

sentences.zh: 有巫託神能禍福人，致貲甚富，均焚像杖巫，出諸境。

translations.literal: There was a shaman who claimed the spirit could bring fortune or disaster to people and amassed great wealth; Jun burned the image, beat the shaman with the staff, and expelled him beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: A shaman claimed that spirits could bless or curse people and grew very rich; Jun burned his image, beat him with a staff, and drove him out of the district.

sentences.zh: 還，監都進奏院。

translations.literal: On his return he supervised the Court Memorial Transmission Office.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made supervisor of the Court Memorial Transmission Office.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，擢開封府推官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended, he was promoted to judicial adjutant of the Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong came to the throne, he was promoted to judicial adjutant of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，復為監察御史。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanyou era he again became Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was again appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 議者請兼用詩賦取士，宰相遂欲廢經義。

translations.literal: Discussers asked to use both poetry and fu in selecting scholars; the chief councillor then wished to abolish the New Text classics examination.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed reviving poetry and fu in the civil service examinations, and the chief councillor then sought to abolish the classics-based examination.

sentences.zh: 均言：「經術以理為主，而所根者本也，詩賦以文為工，而所逐者末也。

translations.literal: Jun said: "Classical learning takes principle as its master, and what it roots in is the fundamental; poetry and fu take literary craft as their skill, and what they pursue is the branch.
translations.idiomatic: Jun argued: "Classical learning is grounded in principle and rests on fundamentals; poetry and fu prize literary craft and chase what is secondary.

sentences.zh: 今不計本末，而欲襲詩賦之敝，未見其為得也。

translations.literal: Now without reckoning root and branch, yet wishing to follow the defects of poetry and fu—I do not see this as gain."
translations.idiomatic: To ignore root and branch and revive the defects of the poetry-and-fu examination would be no gain."

sentences.zh: 」自熙寧以來，京師百司有謁禁。

translations.literal: " Since Xining, the hundred offices of the capital have had prohibitions on visits.
translations.idiomatic: " Since Xining, offices in the capital have been barred from receiving visitors.

sentences.zh: 均言：「以誠待人，則人思竭忠；

translations.literal: Jun said: "If one treats people with sincerity, then people think to exhaust their loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Jun said: "Treat men with sincerity, and they will strive to serve faithfully;

sentences.zh: 以疑遇物，則人思苟免。

translations.literal: if one meets things with suspicion, then people think only to escape blame.
translations.idiomatic: meet them with suspicion, and they will think only of escaping blame.

sentences.zh: 願除開封、大理外，餘皆釋禁，以明洞達不疑之意。

translations.literal: I wish that apart from Kaifeng and the Court of Imperial Appeals, the rest all have the prohibitions released, to make clear the intent of penetrating openness without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that apart from Kaifeng and the Court of Imperial Appeals, all other prohibitions be lifted, to show that the court is open and trusting.

sentences.zh: 」遂論青苗，以為有惠民之名而無惠民之實，有目前之利而為終歲之患，願罷之而復為常平糴糶之法。

translations.literal: " He then discussed the Green Sprouts policy, holding that it had the name of benefiting the people but not the reality, had present profit but became a year's affliction, and wished to abolish it and restore the Ever-Normal Granary purchase-and-sale method.
translations.idiomatic: " He then attacked the Green Sprouts policy, arguing that it bore the name of benefiting the people without the fact, brought short-term gain but year-long harm, and asked that it be abolished in favor of the Ever-Normal Granary purchase-and-sale system.

sentences.zh: 又言官冗之弊，請罷粟補吏，減任子員，節特奏名之濫，增攝官之舉數，抑胥吏之幸進，以清入仕之源。

translations.literal: He also spoke of the defect of official redundancy, asking to abolish grain-supplemented clerks, reduce the quota for sons of officials, restrain the excess of special presentation names, increase the number of acting officials recommended, and suppress the fortunate advancement of petty clerks, to clear the source of entering office.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke against official redundancy, asking to end grain-supplemented clerks, reduce hereditary appointments, curb abuses of special presentation, increase recommendations of acting officials, and restrain petty clerks who advanced by luck, so as to purify the path into office.

sentences.zh: 詔有司議，久之不能有所省。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to discuss it; after a long time they could make no reduction.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the relevant offices to deliberate, but after a long time nothing was reduced.

sentences.zh: 復疏言：「今會議之臣，畏世俗之譏評，不計朝廷之利害，閔鄙耄之不進，不思才者之閑滯，非策之善也。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "The ministers now in conference fear worldly criticism, do not reckon the court's benefit and harm, pity the base and aged who do not advance, and do not think of the talented who are idle and blocked—this is not a good policy."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "The ministers now deliberating fear popular criticism, ignore the court's interests, pity the low-born and elderly who fail to advance, and give no thought to able men left idle—this is no sound policy."

sentences.zh: 」因請對，力陳之，宣仁后曰：「當從我家始。

translations.literal: " He then requested audience and strongly stated his case; Empress Dowager Xuanren said: "It should begin with our house."
translations.idiomatic: " He requested an audience and pressed his case; Empress Dowager Xuanren said, "Let it begin with our own household."

sentences.zh: 」乃自后屬而下至大夫，悉裁其數。

translations.literal: " Thereupon from the empress dowager's kin down to grand masters, all had their numbers reduced.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon appointments were cut from the empress dowager's kin down to grand masters.

sentences.zh: 又言：「治天下道二，寬與猛而已。

translations.literal: He also said: "There are two ways to govern all under heaven—lenience and severity alone.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "There are only two ways to govern the empire—lenience and severity.

sentences.zh: 寬過則緩而傷義，猛過則急而傷恩。

translations.literal: Lenience in excess is lax and injures righteousness; severity in excess is harsh and injures grace.
translations.idiomatic: Excessive lenience grows lax and harms justice; excessive severity grows harsh and harms mercy.

sentences.zh: 術雖不同，其蠹政害民一也。

translations.literal: Though the methods differ, their spoiling governance and harming the people are one.
translations.idiomatic: Though the methods differ, both spoil government and harm the people alike.

sentences.zh: 間者，監司務為慘核，郡縣望風趣辦，不暇以便民為意。

translations.literal: Recently, supervisory commissioners strove for harsh scrutiny; prefectures and counties watched the wind and rushed to complete tasks, with no leisure to make benefiting the people their intent.
translations.idiomatic: Lately supervisory commissioners have pursued harsh scrutiny; prefectures and counties rush to comply and have no thought for the people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨御，務從寬大，為吏者又復苟簡縱弛，猛寬二者胥失。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has taken the throne and strives for lenience and magnanimity, yet those who serve as officials again are perfunctory and lax—both severity and lenience are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has sought lenience and magnanimity, yet officials have again grown perfunctory and lax—both severity and lenience have been lost.

sentences.zh: 願明詔四方，使之寬不縱惡，猛不傷惠，以起中和之風。

translations.literal: I wish a clear edict to the four quarters, causing them to be lenient without indulging evil, severe without injuring grace, to raise the wind of the mean.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a clear edict go to the realm, so that lenience does not indulge evil and severity does not harm mercy, and the spirit of the mean may rise again.

sentences.zh: 」詔下其章。

translations.literal: " An edict was issued transmitting his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne ordered his memorial circulated.

sentences.zh: 蔡確弟碩盜貸官錢以萬計，獄既上，均論確為宰相，挾邪撓法，當顯正其罪，以厲百官。

translations.literal: Cai Que's younger brother Shuo embezzled and lent official funds in tens of thousands; when the case was submitted, Jun argued that Que as chief councillor embraced wickedness and obstructed the law, and his crime should be openly corrected to admonish the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que's younger brother Shuo embezzled tens of thousands in official funds; when the case was submitted, Jun argued that Que, as chief councillor, had embraced wickedness and obstructed the law, and that his crime should be openly punished to warn all officials.

sentences.zh: 張璪、李清臣執政，與正人異趣，相繼擊去之。

translations.literal: Zhang Zan and Li Qingchen held power, differed in tendency from upright men, and he successively attacked and drove them out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zan and Li Qingchen held power and differed from upright men in policy; he successively attacked and drove them from office.

sentences.zh: 監察御史張舜民論邊事，因及宰相文彥博，舜民左遷。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Zhang Shunmin discussed border affairs and thereby touched on Chief Councillor Wen Yanbo; Shunmin was demoted to the left.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Zhang Shunmin discussed border affairs and mentioned Chief Councillor Wen Yanbo; Shunmin was demoted.

sentences.zh: 均言：「風憲之任許風聞，所以廣耳目也。

translations.literal: Jun said: "The duty of censorial discipline permits hearsay, in order to broaden ears and eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Jun said: "The censor's duty permits hearsay precisely to widen the court's eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 舜民之言是，當行之；

translations.literal: If Shunmin's words are right, they should be carried out;
translations.idiomatic: If Shunmin is right, his counsel should be followed;

sentences.zh: 其言非，當容之。

translations.literal: if his words are wrong, he should be tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: if he is wrong, he should still be tolerated.

sentences.zh: 願復舜民職。

translations.literal: I wish Shunmin's post restored.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Shunmin be restored to office.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " The court did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " The court did not agree.

sentences.zh: 臺諫約再論，均謂事小不當再論，王岩叟遂劾均反覆，岩叟移官。

translations.literal: The censorate and remonstrance bureau agreed to debate again; Jun said the matter was small and should not be debated again; Wang Yansou then impeached Jun for inconsistency, and Yansou was transferred.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate agreed to debate the matter again; Jun said the affair was too small to revisit; Wang Yansou then impeached Jun for inconsistency, and Yansou was transferred.

sentences.zh: 均遷殿中侍御史，內不自安，引義丐去，改禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Jun was transferred to Palace Attendant Censor; inwardly ill at ease, he cited principle and begged to leave, and was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was promoted to Palace Attendant Censor but felt uneasy within; citing principle, he asked to resign and was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 居三年，復為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: After three years he again became Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was again appointed Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 西夏自永樂之戰，怙勝氣驕，欲復故地。

translations.literal: Since the battle of Yongle, Western Xia, relying on victory, grew arrogant in spirit and wished to recover its former territory.
translations.idiomatic: Since the battle of Yongle, Western Xia, emboldened by victory, had grown arrogant and sought to recover its former territory.

sentences.zh: 朝廷用趙禼計，棄四砦，至是，又請蘭州為砦地。

translations.literal: The court adopted Zhao Xu's plan and abandoned four fortresses; by this time they again asked that Lanzhou be made fortress territory.
translations.idiomatic: The court had adopted Zhao Xu's plan and abandoned four fortresses; now the Xia again asked that Lanzhou be made fortress territory.

sentences.zh: 均上疏曰：「先王之御外國，知威之不可獨立，故假惠以濟威，知惠之不可獨行，故須威以行惠，然後外國且懷且畏，無怨望輕侮之心。

translations.literal: Jun memorialized: "The former kings in governing foreign states knew that awe could not stand alone, therefore they borrowed grace to assist awe; knew that grace could not act alone, therefore they needed awe to carry out grace—only then did foreign states both cherish and fear, without hearts of resentment, longing, or contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Jun memorialized: "The former kings knew that awe alone could not govern foreign peoples, and so they joined grace to awe; they knew that grace alone could not prevail, and so they joined awe to grace. Only then did foreign states both cherish and fear the court, without resentment or contempt.

sentences.zh: 今西夏所爭蘭州砦地，皆控扼要路，若輕以予之，恐夏人搗虛，熙河數郡，孤立難守。

translations.literal: Now the Lanzhou fortress lands Western Xia disputes all control and choke vital routes; if lightly given away, I fear the Xia will strike at weak points, and the several prefectures of Xihe will be isolated and hard to defend.
translations.idiomatic: The Lanzhou fortress lands now in dispute all command vital routes; if we lightly yield them, the Xia may strike at our weak points, and the Xihe prefectures will stand isolated and hard to defend.

sentences.zh: 若繼請熙河故地，將何辭以拒之？

translations.literal: If they next ask for the former lands of Xihe, with what words will we refuse?
translations.idiomatic: If they next demand the old Xihe territories, what grounds will we have to refuse?

sentences.zh: 是傅虎以翼，借寇以兵，不惟無益，祗足為患。

translations.literal: This is giving a tiger wings and lending an enemy troops—not only without benefit, but only sufficient to become a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: This would be giving a tiger wings and arming an enemy—not only useless, but positively dangerous.

sentences.zh: 不如治兵積穀，畫地而守，使夏人曉然知朝廷意也。」

translations.literal: Better to train troops and store grain, draw boundaries and defend, and make the Xia clearly know the court's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Better to train troops, store grain, mark boundaries, and hold our ground, so that the Xia clearly understand the court's intent."

sentences.zh: 時傅堯俞為中書侍郎，許將為左丞，韓忠彥為同知樞密院。

translations.literal: At the time Fu Yaoyu was Vice Director of the Secretariat, Xu Jiang was Left Vice Grand Councillor, and Han Zhongyan was Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Fu Yaoyu was Vice Director of the Secretariat, Xu Jiang was Left Vice Grand Councillor, and Han Zhongyan was Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三人者，論事多同異，俱求罷。

translations.literal: The three men often differed in discussing affairs and all asked to resign.
translations.idiomatic: The three often disagreed in council and all asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 均言：「大臣之任同國休戚，廟堂之上當務協諧，使中外之人，泯然不知有同異之跡。

translations.literal: Jun said: "The burden of grand ministers shares the state's weal and woe; in the hall of state one should strive for harmony, causing men within and without to be oblivious that traces of difference exist.
translations.idiomatic: Jun said: "Grand ministers share the state's weal and woe; in council they should strive for harmony, so that men within and without no longer perceive factional traces.

sentences.zh: 若悻悻然辨論，不顧事體，何以觀視百僚。

translations.literal: If one resentfully debates without regard for the substance of affairs, how can the hundred officials look on?
translations.idiomatic: If they debate resentfully without regard for the public good, what example do they set for the bureaucracy?

sentences.zh: 堯俞等雖有辨論之失，然事皆緣公，無顯惡大過，望令就職。

translations.literal: Though Yaoyu and the others had the fault of debate, yet their affairs all sprang from public interest, without manifest wickedness or great error; I hope they may be ordered to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yaoyu and the others quarreled, their motives were public and they committed no grave wrong; I ask that they be ordered back to office.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞蘇轍等尚以為言，均上疏曰：「進退大臣當，則天下服陛下之明，而大臣得以安其位。

translations.literal: Chief Censor Su Zhe and others still spoke on it; Jun memorialized: "If advancing and retiring grand ministers is fitting, then all under heaven will submit to Your Majesty's clarity, and grand ministers can settle their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Censor Su Zhe and others still objected; Jun memorialized: "When the promotion and dismissal of ministers is just, the realm will admire Your Majesty's discernment and ministers can rest secure in office.

sentences.zh: 進退不當，則累陛下之哲，而言者自此得以朋黨，合謀並力，以傾搖大臣。

translations.literal: If advancement and retirement are unfitting, then Your Majesty's wisdom is burdened, and from this speakers can form factions, combine plots and join strength, to shake and topple grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When it is unjust, Your Majesty's wisdom is impugned, and remonstrators will form factions and combine to overthrow ministers.

sentences.zh: 天下之事，以是非為主。

translations.literal: Affairs of all under heaven take right and wrong as their master.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs under Heaven should be judged by right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 所論若當，雖異，不害其為善；

translations.literal: If what is argued is fitting, though different, it does not harm its being good;
translations.idiomatic: If the argument is sound, difference does not make it wrong;

sentences.zh: 所論若非，雖同，未免為不善。

translations.literal: if what is argued is unfitting, though the same, it cannot avoid being not good.
translations.idiomatic: if the argument is unsound, agreement does not make it right.

sentences.zh: 今堯俞等但不能協和，實無大過。

translations.literal: Now Yaoyu and the others merely could not harmonize; in reality they had no great fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu and the others merely failed to harmonize; they committed no grave fault.

sentences.zh: 蘇轍乃以許將當時已定議，既而背同列之議，獨上論奏。

translations.literal: Su Zhe then took Xu Jiang as having then already settled the discussion, yet afterward betrayed his colleagues' discussion and alone submitted a memorial of argument.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe charged that Xu Jiang had already agreed with his colleagues, then broke with them and memorialized alone.

sentences.zh: 臣以為善則順之，惡則正之，豈在每事唯命，遂非不改，然後為忠邪？

translations.literal: Your servant holds that if good, then follow it; if evil, then correct it—how can loyalty consist in every matter obeying orders alone, persisting in error without change?
translations.idiomatic: I hold that when a policy is good one should follow it, and when it is bad one should correct it—must loyalty mean obeying every order and never changing course?

sentences.zh: 將舍同列之議，上奉聖旨，是能將順其美，不當反以為過惡也。

translations.literal: Jiang abandoned his colleagues' discussion and above presented the sage command—this is the ability to follow and accord with what is fine; it should not on the contrary be taken as fault and evil.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang set aside his colleagues' view and presented the sovereign's command—this is following what is right, and should not be treated as a fault.

sentences.zh: 若使不忠，雖與同列協和，是乃姦臣爾，非朝廷之利也。

translations.literal: If one is disloyal, though he harmonizes with colleagues, this is merely a treacherous minister—not the court's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: If a man is disloyal, harmony with colleagues makes him only a traitor, not a benefit to the court.

sentences.zh: 」將罷，均又言：「呂大防堅強自任，每有差除，同列不敢異，唯許將時有異同。

translations.literal: " As Jiang was about to be dismissed, Jun again said: "Lü Dafang is strong and self-reliant; whenever there are appointments, colleagues dare not differ—only Xu Jiang sometimes had agreement and difference.
translations.idiomatic: " As Jiang was about to be dismissed, Jun added: "Lü Dafang is domineering; on every appointment his colleagues dare not dissent—only Xu Jiang sometimes disagreed.

sentences.zh: 轍素與大防善，盡力排將，期於必勝。

translations.literal: Zhe has long been friendly with Dafang and exhausts his strength to exclude Jiang, expecting certain victory.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe has long been close to Dafang and used all his strength to drive Jiang out, determined to prevail.

sentences.zh: 臣恐綱紀法令，自此敗壞矣。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that statutes and regulations from this will be corrupted and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that law and discipline will from this be corrupted.

sentences.zh: 」因論：「御史，耳目之任；

translations.literal: " He then argued: "Censors bear the duty of ears and eyes;
translations.idiomatic: " He went on: "Censors are the court's eyes and ears;

sentences.zh: 中丞，風憲之長。

translations.literal: the chief censor is head of censorial discipline.
translations.idiomatic: the chief censor heads censorial discipline.

sentences.zh: 轍當公是公非，別白善惡，而不當妄言也。

translations.literal: Zhe should take public right as public right and public wrong as public wrong, distinguish good and evil, and should not speak rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe should judge right and wrong impartially and distinguish good from evil, not speak recklessly.

sentences.zh: 」遂乞罷，出知廣德軍，改提點河北東路刑獄。

translations.literal: " He then begged to resign, was sent out as prefect of Guangde Army, and changed to judicial intendant for Hebei East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " He then asked to resign, was sent out as prefect of Guangde, and was made judicial intendant for Hebei East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，召拜左正言。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng he was summoned and appointed Left Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shaosheng reign he was recalled and appointed Left Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 時大防、轍已罷政，均論大防、轍六罪，並再黜大防，史禍由此起。

translations.literal: At the time Dafang and Zhe had already left government; Jun argued six crimes of Dafang and Zhe, and again demoted Dafang—the historiographical calamity arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: By then Dafang and Zhe had already left office; Jun charged them with six crimes and secured Dafang's further dismissal—the historiographical persecution began from this.

sentences.zh: 又奏罷詩賦，專以經術取士。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to abolish poetry and fu and take scholars exclusively by classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to abolish the poetry-and-fu examination and select scholars solely by classical learning.

sentences.zh: 宰相章惇欲更政事，專黜陟之柄，陰去異己，出吏部尚書彭汝礪知成都府，召朱服為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Zhang Dun wished to change government affairs, monopolize the power of demotion and promotion, and secretly remove those of different intent; he sent out Minister of Personnel Peng Ruli as prefect of Chengdu and summoned Zhu Fu as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Zhang Dun wished to reshape government, monopolize appointments and dismissals, and secretly remove opponents; he sent Minister of Personnel Peng Ruli out as prefect of Chengdu and summoned Zhu Fu as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 均言汝礪不可出，服不可用。

translations.literal: Jun said Ruli should not be sent out and Fu should not be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun said Ruli should not be sent out and Fu was unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 惇怒，遷均為工部員外郎。

translations.literal: Dun was angry and transferred Jun to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Dun was angry and transferred Jun to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋提點京東、淮東刑獄，歷梓州淮南轉運副使、知越州。

translations.literal: Soon he was judicial intendant for Jingdong and Huaidong, passed through Vice Transport Commissioner of Zizhou and Huainan, and was prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was judicial intendant for Jingdong and Huaidong, then served as Vice Transport Commissioner of Zizhou and Huainan and as prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，入為秘書少監，遷起居郎，拜中書舍人、同修國史兼《哲宗實錄》修撰，遷給事中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended, he entered as Vice Director of the Secretariat, was promoted to Recorder of the Emperor's Actions, appointed Secretariat Drafter, co-compiler of the National History and compiler of the Veritable Records of Emperor Zhezong, and promoted to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong came to the throne, Jun entered court as Vice Director of the Secretariat, was promoted to Recorder of the Emperor's Actions, appointed Secretariat Drafter, co-compiler of the National History and compiler of the Veritable Records of Zhezong, and then promoted to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 太學生張寅亮應詔論事，得罪屏斥，均言：「寅亮雖不識忌諱，然志非懷邪。

translations.literal: Imperial University student Zhang Yinliang responded to an edict to discuss affairs, offended and was expelled; Jun said: "Though Yinliang did not know taboos, yet his intent was not to harbor wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial University student Zhang Yinliang responded to an edict to discuss affairs, gave offense, and was expelled; Jun said, "Though Yinliang failed to observe taboos, his intent was not wicked.

sentences.zh: 陛下既招其來，又罪其言，恐沮多士之氣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty both summoned him to come and then punished his words—I fear this will discourage the spirit of many scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty summoned such men forward and then punished their words—I fear this will discourage scholars everywhere.

sentences.zh: 」寅亮得免。

translations.literal: " Yinliang was spared.
translations.idiomatic: " Yinliang was spared.

sentences.zh: 時宰相欲盡循熙、豐法度為紹述以風均，均曰：「法度惟是之從，無彼此之辨。

translations.literal: At the time the chief councillor wished fully to follow Xining and Yuanfeng institutions as continuation to influence Jun; Jun said: "Institutions follow only what is right; there is no distinction of this side or that.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillor then wished to revive Xining and Yuanfeng institutions wholesale as a program of "continuation" and sway Jun; Jun said, "Institutions should follow what is right, not partisan labels.

sentences.zh: 」由是不協，以龍圖閣待制知永興軍，徙襄州。

translations.literal: " For this he was not in accord, and as Dragon Diagram Hall Academician-Awaiting Orders he was prefect of Yongxing Army, then transferred to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Because of this disagreement he was made Dragon Diagram Hall Academician-Awaiting Orders and prefect of Yongxing, then transferred to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，與元祐黨籍，奪職，主管崇禧觀。

translations.literal: In the early Chongning era he was entered on the Yuanyou faction register, stripped of office, and made superintendent of the Chongxi Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chongning he was listed among the Yuanyou faction, stripped of office, and made superintendent of the Chongxi Abbey.

sentences.zh: 政和中，復集賢院修撰、提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era he again became Compiler in the Hall of Assembled Talents and Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenghe era he was again made Compiler in the Hall of Assembled Talents and Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，復龍圖閣待制，致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time he again became Dragon Diagram Hall Academician-Awaiting Orders and retired.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was again made Dragon Diagram Hall Academician-Awaiting Orders and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 來之邵

translations.literal: Lai ZhiShao
translations.idiomatic: Lai ZhiShao

sentences.zh: 來之邵，字祖德，開封咸平人。

translations.literal: Lai ZhiShao, styled Zude, was a native of Xianping in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Lai ZhiShao, courtesy name Zude, came from Xianping in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，由潞州司理參軍為刑部詳斷官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and from judicial adjutant in Luzhou became detailed adjudication officer in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and rose from judicial adjutant in Luzhou to detailed adjudication officer in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，改大理評事，御史中丞黃履薦為監察御史。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng era he was changed to Evaluator in the Court of Imperial Appeals; Chief Censor Huang Lü recommended him as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanfeng he was made Evaluator in the Court of Imperial Appeals; Chief Censor Huang Lü recommended him as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，買倡家女為妾，履劾其汙行，左遷將作丞。

translations.literal: Before long he bought a singing-girl family's daughter as concubine; Lü impeached his filthy conduct and he was demoted to the left as Director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he bought a courtesan's daughter as a concubine; Lü impeached him for misconduct and he was demoted to Director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.

sentences.zh: 進刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 陽翟民蓋漸以訟至有司，之邵二子皆娶蓋氏，誣漸非蓋氏子，以規其貲。

translations.literal: A man of Yangdi named Gai Jian brought a lawsuit to the authorities; ZhiShao's two sons had both married women of the Gai clan, and they slandered Jian as not a son of the Gai clan in order to seize his property.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Yangdi named Gai Jian brought a lawsuit before the authorities; ZhiShao's two sons had both married Gai women and falsely claimed that Jian was not a Gai clansman in order to seize his property.

sentences.zh: 諫官張商英論之，以直龍圖閣出知蔡州。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Zhang Shangying discussed this; he was given Direct Access to the Dragon Diagram Hall and sent out as prefect of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Zhang Shangying attacked him; he was given Direct Access to the Dragon Diagram Hall and sent out as prefect of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: He died at forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 蔡京為相，特贈太中大夫。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing was chief councillor, he was specially posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing was chief councillor, he was posthumously granted the title Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 葉濤，字致遠，處州龍泉人。

translations.literal: Ye Tao, styled Zhiyuan, was a native of Longquan in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Tao, courtesy name Zhiyuan, came from Longquan in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 進士乙科，為國子直講。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the second class and was Lecturer in the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the second class and was appointed Lecturer in the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 虞蕃訟起，濤坐受諸生茶紙免官。

translations.literal: When Yu Fan's lawsuit arose, Tao was punished for accepting tea and paper from students and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yu Fan affair broke, Tao was dismissed from office for taking tea and stationery gifts from students.

sentences.zh: 濤，王氏婿也，即往從安石於金陵，學為文詞。

translations.literal: Tao was a son-in-law of the Wang clan; he immediately went to follow Anshi at Jinling and studied literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was married into the Wang family; he went at once to study literary composition under Anshi at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，上章自理，得太學正，遷博士。

translations.literal: When Zhezong ascended, he submitted a memorial in self-defense, obtained the post of Director of the Imperial University, and was transferred to Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong came to the throne, he memorialized in his own defense, was restored as Director of the Imperial University, and was promoted to Erudite.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，為秘書省正字，編修《神宗史》，進校書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng he served as Corrector in the Secretariat, compiled the History of Emperor Shenzong, and was advanced to Collator.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaosheng he became Corrector in the Secretariat, helped compile the History of Emperor Shenzong, and was promoted to Collator.

sentences.zh: 曾布薦為起居舍人，擢中書舍人。

translations.literal: Zeng Bu recommended him as Attendant Secretary for Daily Records and he was elevated to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu recommended him as Attendant Secretary for Daily Records, and he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 司馬光、呂公著、王岩叟追貶，呂大防、劉摯、蘇轍、梁燾、范純仁責官，皆濤為制詞，文極醜詆。

translations.literal: Sima Guang, Lü Gongzhu, and Wang Yansou were posthumously demoted; Lü Dafang, Liu Zhi, Su Zhe, Liang Tao, and Fan Chunren were stripped of rank—all were edicts Tao drafted, and the language was extremely vilifying.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang, Lü Gongzhu, and Wang Yansou were posthumously demoted; Lü Dafang, Liu Zhi, Su Zhe, Liang Tao, and Fan Chunren were stripped of rank—for every one of these, Tao drafted the edict text, and his language was savagely abusive.

sentences.zh: 安燾降學士，濤封還命書，云：「燾在元祐時，嘗詆文彥博棄熙河，全先帝萬世之功，不宜加罪。

translations.literal: When An Tao was demoted from Academician, Tao sealed and returned the appointment document, saying: "During Yuanyou, Tao once criticized Wen Yanbo for abandoning Xihe and forfeiting the late emperor's achievements for ten thousand generations; he should not be punished."
translations.idiomatic: When An Tao was demoted from Academician, Tao returned the appointment document sealed, writing: "During Yuanyou, An once condemned Wen Yanbo for abandoning Xihe and throwing away the late emperor's lasting achievements; he ought not to be punished."

sentences.zh: 」蔡京劾為黨，罷知光州。

translations.literal: Cai Jing impeached him as a faction member; he was dismissed and made prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing impeached him as a factionary; he was removed from office and appointed prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又以訴理有過，為范鏜所論，連三黜。

translations.literal: Also because his appeal for redress had errors, he was attacked by Fan Tang and demoted three times in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He was also faulted for mistakes in an appeal for redress; Fan Tang attacked him, and he suffered three successive demotions.

sentences.zh: 曾布引為給事中，居數月而病，以龍閣閣待制提舉崇禧觀，卒。

translations.literal: Zeng Bu brought him in as Supervising Secretary; after several months he fell ill and was made Dragon Diagram Hall Academician-Awaiting Orders and superintendent of the Chongxi Abbey; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu had him appointed Supervising Secretary; after several months he fell ill, was made Dragon Diagram Hall Academician-Awaiting Orders and superintendent of the Chongxi Abbey, and died.

sentences.zh: 楊畏，字子安，其先遂寧人，父徙洛陽。

translations.literal: Yang Wei, styled Zian, his ancestors were from Suining; his father moved to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei, courtesy name Zian, came from Suining by ancestry; his father relocated to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 畏幼孤好學，事母孝，不事科舉。

translations.literal: Wei was orphaned young and loved learning; he served his mother filially and did not pursue the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Wei loved learning, served his mother devotedly, and refused to take the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 黨友交勸之，乃擢進士第。

translations.literal: Party friends repeatedly urged him, and he finally passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Friends in his circle kept pressing him, and he finally passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 調成紀主簿，不之官，刻志經術，以所著書謁王安石、呂惠卿，為鄆州教授。

translations.literal: He was assigned as chief clerk in Chengji but did not take up the post; he devoted himself to the classics and, presenting his writings to Wang Anshi and Lü Huiqing, became professor in Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned chief clerk in Chengji, he never took up the post; he devoted himself to the classics, presented his writings to Wang Anshi and Lü Huiqing, and was appointed professor in Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 自是尊安石之學，以為得聖人之意。

translations.literal: From then on he honored Anshi's learning, taking it to grasp the sage's intent.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he upheld Anshi's learning, believing it captured the true intent of the sages.

sentences.zh: 除西京國子監教授，舒亶薦為監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: He was appointed professor at the Western Capital Directorate of Education; Shu Dan recommended him as Supervising Censor in probationary status.
translations.idiomatic: He was made professor at the Western Capital Directorate of Education; Shu Dan recommended him as probationary Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 時有御史中丞出為郡守，監司薦之，畏言：「侍從賢否，上所素知，監司乃敢妄薦，蓋為異日地爾，乞戒其觀望。

translations.literal: At the time a Vice Censor-in-Chief was going out as prefect, and supervisory officials recommended him; Wei said: "Whether attendants are worthy the emperor already knows well; for supervisory officials to dare recommend recklessly is surely laying groundwork for future favor. I ask that their calculating hesitation be warned against."
translations.idiomatic: When a Vice Censor-in-Chief was leaving the capital to govern a prefecture, circuit officials recommended his successor; Wei protested: "The emperor already knows which attendants are worthy; for circuit officials to recommend people at will is clearly to lay groundwork for future favor. I ask that such hedging ambition be warned against."

sentences.zh: 」舒亶有盜學士院廚錢罪，為王安禮所白，畏抗章辨論，以為可謂之失，未可謂之故。

translations.literal: Shu Dan had a crime of stealing money from the Hanlin Academy kitchens; Wang Anli reported it; Wei submitted a resolute memorial arguing, holding that it could be called a lapse but could not be called deliberate offense.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Dan had stolen money from the Hanlin Academy kitchens; Wang Anli exposed the crime; Wei submitted a forceful memorial arguing that the act could be called a lapse but not a deliberate offense.

sentences.zh: 亶罷，畏坐左轉宗正丞，出提點夔州路刑獄。

translations.literal: When Dan was dismissed, Wei was punished by being transferred left to Director of the Imperial Clan Court and sent out as judicial intendant for Kuizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan was dismissed, Wei was demoted to Director of the Imperial Clan Court and sent out as judicial intendant for Kuizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，請祠歸洛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, he requested a temple post and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou he requested a temple appointment and returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 畏恐得罪於司馬光，嘗曰：「畏官夔峽，雖深山群獠，聞用司馬光，皆相賀，其盛德如此。

translations.literal: Wei feared offending Sima Guang and once said: "When I was official in the Kui Gorge region, even deep-mountain tribal peoples, hearing Sima Guang was employed, all congratulated one another—such was his great virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Fearful of offending Sima Guang, Wei once said: "When I held office in the Kui Gorge, even tribal peoples in deep mountains, on hearing that Sima Guang had been employed, congratulated one another—such was his towering virtue."

sentences.zh: 」至光卒，畏復曰：「司馬光若知道，便是皋、夔、稷、契；

translations.literal: When Guang died, Wei again said: "If Sima Guang had known the Way, he would have been Gao Yao, Kui, Ji, and Qi;"
translations.idiomatic: After Guang died, Wei remarked: "If Sima Guang had truly known the Way, he would have ranked with Gao Yao, Kui, Ji, and Qi;"

sentences.zh: 以不知道，故於政事未盡也。

translations.literal: because he did not know the Way, his handling of affairs was not complete."
translations.idiomatic: because he did not know the Way, his handling of affairs fell short."

sentences.zh: 」呂大防、劉摯為相，俱與畏善，用畏為工部員外郎，除監察御史，擢殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Lü Dafang and Liu Zhi were chief councillors; both were friendly with Wei; he was used as Vice Director in the Ministry of Works, made Supervising Censor, and elevated to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Dafang and Liu Zhi served as chief councillors, both were on good terms with Wei; he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works, then Supervising Censor, then elevated to Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 畏助大防攻摯十事，並言梁燾、王岩叟、劉安世、朱光庭皆其死黨，必與為地。

translations.literal: Wei helped Dafang attack Zhi on ten counts, also saying Liang Tao, Wang Yansou, Liu Anshi, and Zhu Guangting were all his diehard faction and must be dealt with accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Wei helped Dafang attack Zhi on ten counts, and further claimed that Liang Tao, Wang Yansou, Liu Anshi, and Zhu Guangting were Zhi's diehard allies—all of whom had to be removed.

sentences.zh: 既而燾等果救摯，皆不納。

translations.literal: Before long Tao and the others indeed tried to save Zhi, but none was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tao and the others did indeed move to save Zhi, but all were ignored.

sentences.zh: 摯罷，蘇頌為相，畏復攻頌，以留賈易除書為頌罪。

translations.literal: When Zhi was dismissed, Su Song became chief councillor; Wei again attacked Song, taking retention of Jia Yi's appointment document as Song's crime.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhi's dismissal, Su Song became chief councillor; Wei attacked Song again, citing his withholding of Jia Yi's appointment document as a crime.

sentences.zh: 頌罷，畏意欲蘇轍為相。

translations.literal: When Song was dismissed, Wei wished Su Zhe to be chief councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Once Song was out, Wei wanted Su Zhe made chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 宣仁后外召范純仁為右僕射，畏又攻純仁，不報。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren summoned Fan Chunren from outside as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Wei again attacked Chunren, without response.
