translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren summoned Fan Chunren from outside the court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Wei attacked Chunren again, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 畏本附轍，知轍不相，復上疏詆轍不可用。

translations.literal: Wei had originally attached himself to Zhe; learning Zhe would not become chief councillor, he again submitted a memorial vilifying Zhe as unfit for use.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had originally attached himself to Zhe; when he learned Zhe would not become chief councillor, he submitted another memorial denouncing Zhe as unfit for high office.

sentences.zh: 其傾危反覆如此，百僚莫不側目。

translations.literal: His subversive reversals were like this; the hundred officials all looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: Such were his treacherous reversals; the entire bureaucracy looked on in distaste.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，畏言事之未治有四：曰邊疆，曰河事，曰役法，曰內外官政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor; Wei said four matters were still ungoverned: borders, river affairs, corvée law, and internal and external official administration.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Attending Censor, Wei argued that four major areas remained unresolved: the frontier, river affairs, corvée law, and the administration of officials at court and in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 時有旨令兩省官舉臺官，畏言：「御史與宰執，最為相關之地。

translations.literal: At the time there was an order that officials of the two secretariats recommend censorial officials; Wei said: "Censors and chief councillors occupy the most mutually related ground."
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered officials of the two secretariats to recommend censorial appointees; Wei objected: "Censors and chief councillors occupy the most closely intertwined posts."

sentences.zh: 宰執既不自差，使其屬舉之，可乎？

translations.literal: If the chief councillors do not make the appointments themselves but have their subordinates recommend, is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: If the chief councillors will not make the appointments themselves but leave recommendations to their subordinates, how can that be acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 」太常博士朱彥以議皇地示祭不同，自列乞罷。

translations.literal: Director of Ritual Studies Zhu Yan, disagreeing on the imperial earth deity sacrifice ritual, petitioned on his own to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yan, a Director of Ritual Studies, disputed the imperial earth-deity sacrifice rite and petitioned on his own to resign.

sentences.zh: 畏言：「彥據經論理，若彥罷出，恐自是人務觀望，不敢以守官為義。」

translations.literal: Wei said: "Yan argues from the classics and reason; if Yan is dismissed and goes out, I fear from then on people will all watch which way the wind blows and dare not uphold office as righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said: "Yan argues from the classics and from reason; if Yan is dismissed for it, I fear officials everywhere will watch which way the wind blows and shrink from doing their duty."

sentences.zh: 宣仁后崩，呂大防欲用畏諫議大夫，范純仁以畏非端士，不可，大防乃遷畏禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuanren died, Lü Dafang wished to use Wei as Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master; Fan Chunren held that Wei was not an upright man and could not be used; Dafang then transferred Wei to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dowager Xuanren died, Lü Dafang wanted to appoint Wei Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master; Fan Chunren insisted that Wei was no upright man and could not be used, and Dafang instead transferred him to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 及大防為宣仁后山陵使，畏首背大防，稱述熙寧、元豐政事與王安石學術，哲宗信之，遂薦章惇、呂惠卿可大任。

translations.literal: When Dafang served as director of Xuanren's tomb works, Wei was first to turn against Dafang, praising Xining and Yuanfeng administration and Wang Anshi's learning; Zhezong trusted him, and he recommended Zhang Dun and Lü Huiqing for great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: While Dafang directed the empress dowager's tomb works, Wei was the first to turn on him, praising Xining and Yuanfeng policy and Wang Anshi's learning; Zhezong believed him, and Wei recommended Zhang Dun and Lü Huiqing for major posts.

sentences.zh: 廷試進士，李清臣發策有紹述意，考官第主元祐者居上，畏復考，悉下之，拔畢漸以為第一。

translations.literal: At the palace examination for jinshi graduates, Li Qingchen's policy questions had a "continuation" intent; the examiners ranked those favoring Yuanyou at the top; Wei regraded the papers, demoted them all, and elevated Bi Jian to first place.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination, Li Qingchen's policy questions signaled a "continuation" agenda; the examiners had ranked Yuanyou sympathizers at the top; Wei regraded the papers, pushed them all down, and placed Bi Jian first.

sentences.zh: 惇入相，畏遣所親陰結之，曰：「畏前日度勢力之輕重，遂因呂大防、蘇轍以逐劉摯、梁燾。

translations.literal: When Dun entered the chief councillorship, Wei sent a close associate to connect with him secretly, saying: "Wei previously gauged the weight of power and accordingly used Lü Dafang and Su Zhe to drive out Liu Zhi and Liang Tao."
translations.idiomatic: When Dun became chief councillor, Wei sent a confidant to reach him in secret, saying: "Wei once gauged where power lay and, through Lü Dafang and Su Zhe, drove out Liu Zhi and Liang Tao."

sentences.zh: 方欲逐呂、蘇，二人覺，罷畏言職。

translations.literal: Just as he was about to drive out Lü and Su, the two perceived it and had Wei's remonstrance office stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was moving against Lü and Su, the two caught on and had him stripped of his remonstrance post.

sentences.zh: 畏跡在元祐，心在熙寧，首為相公開路者也。

translations.literal: Wei's traces were in Yuanyou but his heart was in Xining—he was the first to open the way for the chief councillor."
translations.idiomatic: Wei's footprints were in Yuanyou, but his heart was in Xining—he was the first to clear the chief councillor's path."

sentences.zh: 」惇至，徙畏吏部，引以自助。

translations.literal: When Dun arrived, he transferred Wei to the Ministry of Personnel and brought him in to help himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Dun took power, he moved Wei to the Ministry of Personnel and brought him in as an ally.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎李清臣、知樞密院安燾與惇不合，畏復陰附安、李，惇覺其情；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Qingchen and Military Affairs Commissioner An Tao were at odds with Dun; Wei again secretly attached himself to An and Li; Dun perceived his real allegiance;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Qingchen and Military Affairs Commissioner An Tao were at odds with Dun; Wei again covertly aligned with An and Li; Dun saw through him;

sentences.zh: 又曾布、蔡卞言畏平日所為於惇，遂以寶文閣待制出知真定府。

translations.literal: also Zeng Bu and Cai Bian spoke of Wei's daily conduct toward Dun, and he was made Academician-Awaiting Orders of the Baowen Pavilion and sent out as prefect of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: and when Zeng Bu and Cai Bian recounted Wei's habitual double-dealing toward Dun, he was made Academician-Awaiting Orders of the Baowen Pavilion and sent out to govern Zhending.

sentences.zh: 天下於是目為「楊三變」，謂其進於元豐，顯於元祐，遷於紹聖也。

translations.literal: All under Heaven then labeled him "Yang the Thrice-Changing," saying he advanced in Yuanfeng, stood out in Yuanyou, and shifted in Shaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: The empire then nicknamed him "Yang the Thrice-Changing," saying he had risen in Yuanfeng, shone in Yuanyou, and switched sides in Shaosheng.

sentences.zh: 尋落職知虢州，入元祐黨。

translations.literal: Before long he was demoted and made prefect of Guo, and entered the Yuanyou faction register.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was demoted to prefect of Guo and listed on the Yuanyou faction register.

sentences.zh: 後知郢州，復集賢殿修撰、知襄州，移荊南，提舉洞霄宮，居於洛。

translations.literal: Later he was prefect of Yingzhou, again became Compiler at the Hall for Collecting Worthies and prefect of Xiangzhou, moved to Jingnan, and was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Abbey, residing in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Yingzhou, was again made Compiler at the Hall for Collecting Worthies and prefect of Xiangzhou, moved to Jingnan, and was appointed superintendent of the Dongxiao Abbey, living in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知鄧州，再丐祠，以言者論列落職，主管崇禧觀。

translations.literal: Before long he was prefect of Dengzhou; he twice begged for a temple post; because remonstrators criticized him he was demoted and made superintendent of the Chongxi Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was prefect of Dengzhou; he twice begged for a temple appointment; critics brought him down again, and he was made superintendent of the Chongxi Abbey.

sentences.zh: 蔡京為相，畏遣子侄見京，以元祐末論蘇轍不可大用等章自明，又因京黨河南尹薛昂致言於京，遂出黨籍。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing was chief councillor, Wei sent his sons and nephews to see Jing, clarifying himself with memorials from the end of Yuanyou that Su Zhe could not be greatly employed and the like, and also through Jing's faction member Xue Ang, chief magistrate of Henan, spoke to Jing; he was then removed from the faction register.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing was chief councillor, Wei sent his sons and nephews to Jing, citing his Yuanyou-era memorials that Su Zhe was unfit for high office to explain himself, and also reached Jing through his ally Xue Ang, chief magistrate of Henan; he was then removed from the faction register.

sentences.zh: 尋復寶文閣待制。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored as Academician-Awaiting Orders of the Baowen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored as Academician-Awaiting Orders of the Baowen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，洛人詣闕，請封禪嵩山，畏上疏累千餘言，極其諛佞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, people of Luoyang went to the capital requesting a feng-shan rite on Mount Song; Wei submitted a memorial of more than a thousand words, flattery of the utmost sycophancy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenghe, Luoyang residents petitioned at court for a feng-shan rite on Mount Song; Wei submitted a memorial of more than a thousand words of the most abject flattery.

sentences.zh: 方治行，得疾卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: Just as his conduct was being assessed, he fell ill and died at sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Just as his fitness for office was under review, he fell ill and died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 畏頗為縱橫學，有才辯而多捭闔，與邢恕締交，其好功名富貴亦同。

translations.literal: Wei was quite versed in coalition studies, had talent and eloquence but much scheming, and formed a friendship with Xing Shu; their craving for fame, rank, and wealth was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was steeped in coalition tactics, gifted and eloquent but endlessly scheming; he bonded with Xing Shu, and both hungered equally for fame, rank, and wealth.

sentences.zh: 然恕疏而多失，畏謀必中，其究俱為搢紳禍雲。

translations.literal: Yet Shu was coarse and often blundered; Wei's plots always hit their mark; in the end both alike brought calamity upon the gentry like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was crude and often blundered; Wei's schemes always landed; in the end both brought disaster on the official class alike.

sentences.zh: 論曰：賈易初以剛直名，觀其再劾文彥博、范純仁，而斥蘇軾、蘇轍尤甚，何以剛直為哉？

translations.literal: Commentary: Jia Yi was first known for blunt uprightness—yet seeing him twice impeach Wen Yanbo and Fan Chunren, and especially reproach Su Shi and Su Zhe, how can this be called uprightness?
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Jia Yi was first known for blunt integrity—yet when one sees him twice impeach Wen Yanbo and Fan Chunren, and attack Su Shi and Su Zhe with special venom, how can he be called upright?

sentences.zh: 董敦逸於元祐末與黃慶基誣二蘇，以開紹聖之禍，及紹聖則肆詆元祐諸臣，甚至瑤華之冤不能持正，雖終悔而諫，亦何及焉。

translations.literal: Dong Dunyi at the end of Yuanyou together with Huang Qingji falsely accused the two Su brothers, opening the calamity of Shaosheng; when Shaosheng came he wantonly vilified Yuanyou ministers, and even in the injustice of Yaohua could not hold to what was right; though he finally repented and remonstrated, what good was it?
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanyou, Dong Dunyi and Huang Qingji falsely accused the two Su brothers, opening the calamity of Shaosheng; when Shaosheng arrived he wantonly reviled the Yuanyou ministers, and even in the injustice done to Princess Yaohua could not stand for what was right; though he finally repented and remonstrated, what good did that do?

sentences.zh: 及見蔡京、蔡卞稔惡，乃論其過惡以自文，杯水不足以救車薪之火也。

translations.literal: Only when he saw Cai Jing and Cai Bian's accumulated wickedness did he discuss their faults to exculpate himself—a cup of water cannot save a cartload of burning firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Only when he saw Cai Jing and Cai Bian's accumulated evil did he denounce their crimes to clear himself—a cup of water cannot quench a cartload of burning kindling.

sentences.zh: 上官均諫切中時事，及不從紹述之議，其為人若可觀，然論呂大防、蘇轍，以之再黜，是亦助紹述者也。

translations.literal: Shang Guanjun's remonstrances keenly hit the affairs of the time, and in not following the "continuation" program his conduct seemed admirable; yet in getting Lü Dafang and Su Zhe demoted a second time, he too aided the "continuation."
translations.idiomatic: Shang Guanjun's remonstrances cut to the heart of current affairs, and in refusing the "continuation" agenda he seemed a man of substance; yet in securing a second demotion for Lü Dafang and Su Zhe, he too served the "continuation" cause.

sentences.zh: 楊畏傾危反覆，周流不窮，雖儀、秦縱橫，無以尚之，豈徒有三變而已。

translations.literal: Yang Wei's subversive reversals flowed on without end—even Yi and Qin in coalition tactics could not surpass him; was it only three changes?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei's treacherous reversals flowed on without end—even the coalition masters Yi and Qin could not surpass him; was it merely three changes?

sentences.zh: 至於倡紹述以取信哲宗，又謂王安石之學有聖人意，可謂小人無忌憚也哉。

translations.literal: As for advocating "continuation" to win Zhezong's trust, and also saying Wang Anshi's learning had the sage's intent, one could call this a petty man utterly without scruple.
translations.idiomatic: To promote "continuation" in order to win Zhezong's trust, and to declare that Wang Anshi's learning captured the sage's intent—such a man may truly be called utterly shameless.

sentences.zh: 來之邵盡擊時賢而進章惇、安燾、呂惠卿，又請加美諡於安石，其流惡不已，乃誣人非其子而欲掩其貲，亦何所不至焉。

translations.literal: Lai ZhiShao attacked all worthy men of the time while advancing Zhang Dun, An Tao, and Lü Huiqing, and also asked to add a posthumous honorific to Anshi; his stream of wickedness did not cease—he even falsely claimed a man was not his father's son to seize his property; what would he not do?
translations.idiomatic: Lai ZhiShao attacked every worthy man of the age while pushing Zhang Dun, An Tao, and Lü Huiqing forward, and even sought a posthumous honorific for Anshi; his stream of wickedness never ceased—he would falsely deny a man's paternity to seize his property; what would he stop at?

sentences.zh: 葉濤在太學，已著汙跡，擢第之後，諂安石而從之學，後得曾布之薦，凡元祐名賢貶責制辭，肆筆醜詆，雖有善猶不能自滌，況無可述者乎！

translations.literal: Ye Tao at the Imperial University already left filthy traces; after passing the examination he flattered Anshi and followed his learning; later through Zeng Bu's recommendation, for every demotion edict of a Yuanyou worthy he wielded the brush in vile abuse—even if he had virtue he still could not cleanse himself, much less when there was nothing to recount!
translations.idiomatic: Ye Tao had already stained his name at the Imperial University; after passing the examination he flattered Anshi and followed his learning; later, through Zeng Bu's patronage, he drafted every edict demoting a Yuanyou worthy in language of vile abuse—even had he possessed virtue he could not have cleansed himself, much less when there was nothing worth recounting!

sentences.zh: 崔台符

translations.literal: Cui Taifu
translations.idiomatic: Cui Taifu

sentences.zh: 崔台符，字平叔，蒲陰人。

translations.literal: Cui Taifu, styled Pingshu, was a native of Puyin.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Taifu, courtesy name Pingshu, came from Puyin.

sentences.zh: 中明法科，為大理詳斷官，校試殿帷，仁宗賜以「盡美」二字。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingfa branch and became detailed adjudication officer in the Court of Imperial Appeals; he was examined in the palace curtain and Renzong bestowed on him the two characters "Perfect in Beauty."
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingfa examination and became detailed adjudication officer in the Court of Imperial Appeals; examined before the palace curtain, Renzong bestowed on him the two characters "Perfect in Beauty."

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，文彥博薦為群牧判官，除河北監牧使，入判大理寺。

translations.literal: In the Xining era Wen Yanbo recommended him as aide in the Office of Herds; he was made Commissioner of Herds for Hebei and entered as vice-director of the Court of Imperial Appeals.
translations.idiomatic: During Xining, Wen Yanbo recommended him as aide in the Office of Herds; he was made Commissioner of Herds for Hebei and entered service as vice-director of the Court of Imperial Appeals.

sentences.zh: 初，王安石定按問欲舉法，舉朝以為非，台符獨舉手加額曰：「數百年誤用刑名，今乃得正。

translations.literal: At first Wang Anshi established the interrogation-to-expose law; the whole court thought it wrong; Taifu alone raised his hands to his forehead and said: "For hundreds of years penal names were wrongly applied; now it is finally set right."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi first established the interrogation-to-expose law, the whole court thought it wrong; Taifu alone raised his hands to his forehead and exclaimed: "For centuries penal law was misapplied; now it is finally set right."

sentences.zh: 」安石喜其附己，故用之。

translations.literal: Anshi was pleased he sided with him and therefore used him.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was pleased that Taifu sided with him and accordingly gave him office.

sentences.zh: 歷知審刑院，判少府監。

translations.literal: He successively served as director of the Office of Review and vice-director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as director of the Office of Review and vice-director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.

sentences.zh: 復置大理獄，拜右諫議大夫，為大理卿。

translations.literal: When the Court of Imperial Appeals prison was restored, he was made Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master and Director of the Court of Imperial Appeals.
translations.idiomatic: When the Court of Imperial Appeals prison was reinstated, he was made Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master and Director of the Court of Imperial Appeals.

sentences.zh: 時中官石得一以皇城偵邏為獄，台符與少卿楊汲輒迎伺其意，所在以鍛煉笞掠成之，都人惴栗，至不敢偶語。

translations.literal: At the time the eunuch Shi Deyi used surveillance patrol of the imperial city as a prison case; Taifu and Vice Director Yang Ji at once welcomed and awaited his intent, everywhere forging cases through torture and beating; the capital people were fearful, to the point they dared not speak even in pairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the eunuch Shi Deyi turned imperial-city patrol duty into a criminal investigation; Taifu and Vice Director Yang Ji at once catered to his wishes, manufacturing convictions through torture and beating wherever they went; the people of the capital were terrified—even pairs dared not speak together.

sentences.zh: 數年間，麗文法者且萬人。

translations.literal: Within several years those entangled in textual law numbered nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years nearly ten thousand people were caught up in charges under the letter of the law.

sentences.zh: 官制行，遷刑部侍郎，官至光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the new official system was implemented, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and reached the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: When the new official system took effect, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and rose to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，御史林旦、上官均發其惡，出知潞州，又貶秩徙相州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, censors Lin Dan and Shang Guanjun exposed his wickedness; he was sent out as prefect of Luzhou and again demoted in rank and moved to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou, censors Lin Dan and Shang Guanjun exposed his crimes; he was sent out as prefect of Luzhou, then demoted again and transferred to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 後兼監牧使。

translations.literal: Later he also served concurrently as Commissioner of Herds.
translations.idiomatic: He later also served concurrently as Commissioner of Herds.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 舊制，武臣至內殿崇班，始蔭其族。

translations.literal: Under the old system, military officials only began to grant hereditary privilege to their clans upon reaching Inner Hall Standard Bearer rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, military officials could begin granting hereditary privilege to their kin only after reaching Inner Hall Standard Bearer rank.

sentences.zh: 台符言：「文吏州判司猶許用蔭，武臣五歲一遷，自借職四十年乃得通朝籍，輕重不相準。

translations.literal: Taifu said: "Civil officials even at prefectural judicial assistants are allowed to use privilege; military officials advance once every five years—from borrowed rank it takes forty years to enter the court register; light and heavy do not match."
translations.idiomatic: Taifu said: "Even a civil official at the level of a prefectural judicial assistant may use hereditary privilege; military officials advance once every five years—it takes forty years from a borrowed rank to enter the court register; the scales of reward do not match."

sentences.zh: 請自供奉官即用蔭。

translations.literal: I ask that from Attendant-in-Waiting rank they may immediately use privilege."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from Attendant-in-Waiting rank they be allowed to use privilege at once."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 嘗使遼，至其朝，久立帳前，儐者不贊導。

translations.literal: Once when he was envoy to Liao, he reached their court and stood long before the tent; the masters of ceremony did not announce him in.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on an embassy to Liao, he reached their court and stood for a long time before the tent; the masters of ceremony did not announce him in.

sentences.zh: 問其故，曰：「太子未至。

translations.literal: He asked the reason; they said: "The crown prince has not yet arrived."
translations.idiomatic: When he asked why, they said: "The crown prince has not yet arrived."

sentences.zh: 」台符誚之曰：「安有君父臨軒而臣子偃蹇不至，久立使者禮乎？

translations.literal: Taifu rebuked them: "How can the lord and father sit on the throne while ministers and sons are negligent and do not come, leaving the envoy standing long—is this ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: Taifu rebuked them: "How can the sovereign be on the throne while ministers and sons hang back and refuse to come, leaving an envoy standing for ages—is that proper ritual?"

sentences.zh: 」儐者懼，贊導如儀。

translations.literal: The masters of ceremony were afraid and announced and guided him according to ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The masters of ceremony, afraid, announced and escorted him in according to proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 楊汲，字潛古，泉州晉江人。

translations.literal: Yang Ji, styled Qian'gu, was a native of Jinjiang in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji, courtesy name Qian'gu, came from Jinjiang in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，調趙州司法參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as judicial adjutant in Zhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned judicial adjutant in Zhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州民曹潯者，兄遇之不善，兄子亦加侮焉。

translations.literal: A man of the prefecture named Cao Xun—his elder brother treated him badly, and the elder brother's son also added insult.
translations.idiomatic: A townsman named Cao Xun was mistreated by his elder brother, and his nephew insulted him as well.

sentences.zh: 潯持刀逐兄子，兄挾之以走，潯曰：「兄勿避，自為侄爾。

translations.literal: Xun took a knife and chased the elder brother's son; the elder brother seized him and fled; Xun said: "Elder brother, do not flee—I meant it for the nephew alone."
translations.idiomatic: Xun took a knife and chased his nephew; his elder brother grabbed him and fled; Xun cried: "Brother, do not run—I was after the nephew alone."

sentences.zh: 」既就吏，兄子云：「叔欲紿吾父，止而殺之。

translations.literal: Once before the officials, the elder brother's son said: "Uncle wanted to deceive my father, stop him, and kill him."
translations.idiomatic: Before the magistrate, the nephew said: "My uncle meant to trick my father into stopping, then kill him."

sentences.zh: 」吏當潯謀殺兄，汲曰：「潯呼兄使勿避，何謂謀？

translations.literal: The clerks judged Xun guilty of plotting to kill his elder brother; Ji said: "Xun called to his elder brother not to flee—how is that plotting?"
translations.idiomatic: The clerks judged Xun guilty of plotting to kill his elder brother; Ji objected: "Xun shouted for his brother not to flee—how is that a plot?"

sentences.zh: 若以意為獄，民無所措手足矣。

translations.literal: If one judges by intent rather than the case, the people will have nowhere to put hand or foot."
translations.idiomatic: If courts try cases by inferred intent rather than evidence, the people will have nowhere to stand."

sentences.zh: 」州用其言，讞上，潯得不死。

translations.literal: The prefecture accepted his view; the report went up and Xun escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture accepted his reasoning; the report went up, and Xun was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 主管開封府界常平，權都水丞，與侯叔獻行汴水淤田法，遂釃汴流漲潦以溉西部，瘠土皆為良田。

translations.literal: He superintended the Kaifeng metropolitan belt Ever-Normal Granary, held acting appointment as Director of the Bureau of Waterways, and with Hou Shuxian implemented the Bian River silt-farming method; they then diverted the Bian's flood to irrigate the western region and poor soil all became good fields.
translations.idiomatic: He superintended the Kaifeng metropolitan Ever-Normal Granary, served as acting Director of the Bureau of Waterways, and with Hou Shuxian implemented the Bian River silt-farming method; they diverted floodwaters from the Bian to irrigate the western districts, turning poor soil into good farmland.

sentences.zh: 神宗嘉之，賜以所淤田千畝。

translations.literal: Shenzong praised this and granted him a thousand mu of the silted land.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong praised the work and granted him a thousand mu of the newly reclaimed land.

sentences.zh: 提點淮西刑獄，提舉西路常平，修古芍陂，引漢泉灌田萬頃。

translations.literal: He was judicial intendant for Huai West Circuit, superintendent of the Western Route Ever-Normal Granary, restored the ancient Shao Marsh, and channeled Han spring water to irrigate ten thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial intendant for Huai West Circuit, superintendent of the Western Route Ever-Normal Granary, restored the ancient Shao Marsh, and channeled Han spring water to irrigate ten thousand qing of fields.

sentences.zh: 召判都水監，為大理卿，遷刑部、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as vice-director of the Directorate of Waterways, became Director of the Court of Imperial Appeals, and was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as vice-director of the Directorate of Waterways, became Director of the Court of Imperial Appeals, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，以寶文閣待制知廬州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was made Academician-Awaiting Orders of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Luz prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou he was made Academician-Awaiting Orders of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Luz.

sentences.zh: 崔台符被劾，汲亦落職知黃州。

translations.literal: When Cui Taifu was impeached, Ji also was demoted and made prefect of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Taifu was impeached, Ji was demoted as well and appointed prefect of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷徐、襄、越州。

translations.literal: He successively served in Xuzhou, Xiangzhou, and Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Xuzhou, Xiangzhou, and Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，復為戶部侍郎，卒。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng era he again served as Vice Minister of Revenue and died.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaosheng he was again made Vice Minister of Revenue, then died.

sentences.zh: 呂嘉問

translations.literal: Lü Jiawen
translations.idiomatic: Lü Jiawen

sentences.zh: 呂嘉問，字望之，以蔭入官。

translations.literal: Lü Jiawen, styled Wangzhi, entered office through yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Jiawen, styled Wangzhi, entered official service through inherited privilege.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，條例司引以為屬，權戶部判官，管諸司庫務，行連灶法於酒坊，歲省薪錢十六萬緡。

translations.literal: In the early Xining era the Regulations Bureau brought him in as a subordinate; he served as acting Revenue Section Chief, managed the treasuries of various offices, implemented the linked-kiln method at wine monopolies, and saved one hundred sixty thousand strings of cash in fuel costs annually.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xining the Regulations Bureau took him on as a subordinate. He served as acting chief of the Revenue Section, oversaw the treasuries of various departments, introduced the linked-kiln method at state wine monopolies, and saved one hundred sixty thousand strings in fuel costs each year.

sentences.zh: 王安石用魏繼宗議，即京城置市易務，命嘉問提舉。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi adopted Wei Jizong's proposal, immediately established the Market Exchange Office in the capital, and appointed Jiawen to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi adopted Wei Jizong's proposal, established the Market Exchange Office in the capital at once, and put Jiawen in charge.

sentences.zh: 上建置十三事，其一欲於律外禁兼並之家輒取利，神宗去之，安石執不可。

translations.literal: He proposed thirteen measures for establishment; one wished to forbid, outside the law, consolidation households from taking profit at will — Shenzong removed it, and Anshi insisted it could not be removed.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed thirteen measures for the new system. One would have forbidden monopolistic families from reaping profits beyond what the law allowed. Shenzong struck it out, but Anshi refused to accept its removal.

sentences.zh: 居二年，連以羨課受賞。

translations.literal: After two years in office, he repeatedly received rewards for surplus revenue quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years he was repeatedly rewarded for exceeding revenue targets.

sentences.zh: 神宗聞其擾民。

translations.literal: Shenzong heard that it harassed the people.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong heard that the system was oppressing the people.

sentences.zh: 語安石。

translations.literal: He spoke to Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke to Anshi about it.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「嘉問奉法不公，以是媒怨。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Jiawen implements the law unfairly, and thereby invites resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi said, "Jiawen enforces the law unfairly, and that is what provokes resentment."

sentences.zh: 」神宗曰：「免行錢所收細瑣，市易鬻及果實，大傷國體。

translations.literal: Shenzong said: "The exemption fee collected is petty and trivial; the Market Exchange even sells fruit — this greatly injures the dignity of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong said, "The exemption fees are petty and intrusive, and the Market Exchange is even peddling fruit — this is a grave blow to the dignity of the court."

sentences.zh: 」安石偽辨自解，至譏神宗為叢脞，不知帝王大略，且曰：「非嘉問，執敢不避左右近習？

translations.literal: Anshi dissembled in self-defense, going so far as to mock Shenzong as petty and ignorant of the emperor's grand design, and also said: "Were it not for Jiawen, who would dare not defer to the favorites at the emperor's side?"
translations.idiomatic: Anshi argued disingenuously in his own defense, even ridiculing Shenzong as small-minded and ignorant of imperial strategy, and said, "Without Jiawen, who would dare stand up to the emperor's close favorites?"

sentences.zh: 非臣，孰為嘉問辨？

translations.literal: Without me, who would argue on Jiawen's behalf?
translations.idiomatic: Without me, who would speak for Jiawen?

sentences.zh: 」神宗曰：「即如是，士大夫何故以為不便？

translations.literal: Shenzong said: "If that is so, why do the scholar-officials consider it inconvenient?"
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong said, "If that is true, why do so many officials find the policy objectionable?"

sentences.zh: 」安石請言者姓名，令嘉問條析。

translations.literal: Anshi asked for the names of those who spoke and had Jiawen analyze them item by item.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi asked for the names of the critics and had Jiawen refute each charge in detail.

sentences.zh: 七年，旱，帝憂心惻怛，語韓維、孫永集市人問之，減坐賈錢千萬。

translations.literal: In the seventh year there was drought; the emperor was deeply troubled at heart, had Han Wei and Sun Yong gather market traders to question them, and reduced the sitting-merchant fee by ten million.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year drought struck. The emperor was deeply troubled and sent Han Wei and Sun Yong to question market traders; the sitting-merchant fee was cut by ten million cash.

sentences.zh: 安石遂持嘉問條析奏曰：「此皆百姓所願，不如人言也。

translations.literal: Anshi then submitted Jiawen's itemized analysis, saying: "These are all what the common people wish — not as people say."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi then submitted Jiawen's detailed rebuttal, saying, "These measures are what the people themselves want — not what the critics claim."

sentences.zh: 」嘉問言：「朝廷所以許民輸錢免行者，蓋人情安於樂業，厭於追擾，若一切罷去，則無人祗承。

translations.literal: Jiawen said: "The reason the court allows the people to pay money to be exempt from corvée travel is that human sentiment prefers secure livelihood and dislikes pursuit and harassment; if all were abolished at once, no one would undertake the duties."
translations.idiomatic: Jiawen said, "The court allows people to pay a fee in lieu of courier duty because ordinary folk want steady livelihoods and hate being hounded by officials. Abolish the system entirely and no one will take up the work."

sentences.zh: 又吏胥祿廩薄，勢不得不求於民，非重法莫禁。

translations.literal: Moreover the salaries and rations of clerks and runners are thin; they are bound to demand from the people, and only strict law can forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, clerks and runners are so poorly paid that they cannot help extorting the people; only stern law can restrain them.

sentences.zh: 以薄廩申重法，則法有時而不行。

translations.literal: To apply strict law on the basis of thin rations is to have law that sometimes fails to be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Strict laws backed by meager pay yield laws that are honored only when convenient.

sentences.zh: 縣官為給事，則三司經費有限，今取民於鮮，而吏知自重，此臣等推行之本意也。

translations.literal: If the county officials supplied the service, the Three Departments' funds would be limited; now revenue is taken in small amounts from the people, and officials know to respect themselves — this is the original intent of us ministers in carrying it out.
translations.idiomatic: If county officials paid for the service, the Three Departments' budget could not bear it. By collecting modest fees from the people and giving officials decent support, we aim to make them conduct themselves properly — that was always our intent.

sentences.zh: 議者乃欲除去，是殆不然。

translations.literal: Those who discuss the matter wish to abolish it — this is probably not correct.
translations.idiomatic: Critics who want to abolish the fees have it wrong.

sentences.zh: 民未嘗不畏吏，方其以行役觸罪，雖欲出錢，亦不可得。

translations.literal: The people have never failed to fear officials; when they commit offenses in corvée travel, even if they wish to pay money, they cannot obtain exemption.
translations.idiomatic: The people have always feared officials. When they run afoul of corvée regulations, they cannot buy their way out even if they wish to.

sentences.zh: 今吏祿可謂厚矣，然未及昔日取民所得之半，市易所收免行錢，亦未足以償倉法所增之祿，以此推窮，則利害立見矣。」

translations.literal: Now officials' salaries may be called generous, yet they do not reach half of what was formerly taken from the people; the exemption fees collected by the Market Exchange also do not suffice to repay the increased salaries under the granary system — pursue this to the end and benefit and harm stand clear at once."
translations.idiomatic: Officials' pay is generous by past standards, yet it is still less than half what clerks once extorted from the people. The exemption fees the Market Exchange collects do not even cover the salary increases under the granary reform. Push the calculation that far and the balance of costs and benefits becomes obvious."

sentences.zh: 初，市易隸三司，嘉問恃勢陵使薛向，出其上。

translations.literal: At first the Market Exchange was subordinate to the Three Departments; Jiawen relied on power to override and bully Commissioner Xue Xiang, placing himself above him.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Market Exchange fell under the Three Departments. Jiawen used his backing to bully Commissioner Xue Xiang and set himself above him.

sentences.zh: 曾布代向，懷不能平。

translations.literal: Zeng Bu replaced Xiang and harbored resentment that he could not reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Bu replaced Xiang, he seethed at the insult.

sentences.zh: 會神宗出手劄詢布，布訪於魏繼宗，繼宗憤嘉問掠其功，列其與初議異者。

translations.literal: It happened that Shenzong handed down a personal note inquiring of Bu; Bu consulted Wei Jizong, and Jizong, angered that Jiawen had seized his credit, listed points where Jiawen differed from the original proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong sent Bu a personal note of inquiry. Bu consulted Wei Jizong, who, bitter that Jiawen had stolen his credit, listed every point on which Jiawen had diverged from the original plan.

sentences.zh: 布得實，具上嘉問多收息干賞，挾官府而為兼并之事。

translations.literal: Bu obtained the facts and fully reported that Jiawen repeatedly collected surplus interest to seek rewards and wielded official power to carry out monopolistic consolidation.
translations.idiomatic: Bu verified the facts and reported that Jiawen had repeatedly inflated profits to win rewards and used government power to engage in monopolistic consolidation.

sentences.zh: 神宗將委布考之，安石言二人有私忿，於是詔布與呂惠卿同 治。

translations.literal: Shenzong was about to entrust Bu to investigate; Anshi said the two men had private resentment, and so the edict ordered Bu and Lü Huiqing to investigate jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong was about to put Bu in charge of the inquiry, but Anshi said the two men bore a private grudge. An edict then ordered Bu and Lü Huiqing to investigate together.

sentences.zh: 惠卿故憾布，至三司，召繼宗及市賈問狀，其辭同，乃脅繼宗使誣布語言增加，繼宗不從。

translations.literal: Huiqing had long resented Bu; arriving at the Three Departments, he summoned Jizong and market traders to question the facts — their accounts agreed — then coerced Jizong to falsely charge that Bu had added to his words; Jizong would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing already hated Bu. At the Three Departments he summoned Jizong and market traders; their stories matched, so he tried to force Jizong to accuse Bu of embellishing his testimony. Jizong refused.

sentences.zh: 布言惠卿不可共事，神宗欲聽之，安石不可。

translations.literal: Bu said Huiqing could not serve together with him; Shenzong wished to allow this, but Anshi would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Bu declared he could not work with Huiqing. Shenzong was inclined to agree, but Anshi objected.

sentences.zh: 神宗遂詔中書曰：「朝廷設市易，本為平準以便民，若《周官》泉府者。

translations.literal: Shenzong then issued an edict to the Secretariat saying: "The court established the Market Exchange originally to stabilize prices and benefit the people, like the Quanfu of the Zhou Offices."
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong then directed the Secretariat: "The Market Exchange was meant to stabilize prices and serve the people, on the model of the Quanfu bureau in the Rites of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 今顧使中人之家失業，宜厘定其制。

translations.literal: Now it plainly causes middling households to lose their livelihoods — the system should be regulated and fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Instead it is driving ordinary shopkeepers out of business. The regulations must be revised."

sentences.zh: 」布見神宗曰：「臣每聞德音，欲以王道治天下，今所為駸駸乎間架、除陌矣。

translations.literal: Bu saw Shenzong and said: "Whenever I hear Your Majesty's gracious words, I wish to govern all under Heaven by the royal way; what is done now is steadily becoming like the Jianjia and Chumo taxes."
translations.idiomatic: Bu told Shenzong, "Your gracious pronouncements promise governance by the royal way, yet our policies are sliding toward the hated Jianjia and Chumo levies of old."

sentences.zh: 嘉問又請販鹽鬻帛，豈不詒四方笑？

translations.literal: Jiawen further requested to sell salt and trade silk — would this not invite laughter from all quarters?
translations.idiomatic: Jiawen even wants the state to peddle salt and sell cloth. Will that not make us a laughingstock across the realm?"

sentences.zh: 」神宗頷之。

translations.literal: Shenzong nodded in agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong nodded in agreement.

sentences.zh: 事未決，安石去位，嘉問持之以泣，安石勞之曰：「吾已薦惠卿矣。

translations.literal: Before the matter was decided, Anshi left office; Jiawen grasped his hand and wept; Anshi consoled him, saying: "I have already recommended Huiqing."
translations.idiomatic: Before the matter was settled, Anshi left office. Jiawen seized his hand in tears. Anshi comforted him: "I have already recommended Huiqing."

sentences.zh: 」惠卿既執政，前獄遂成，布得罪，嘉問亦出知常州。

translations.literal: Once Huiqing held power, the earlier case was concluded; Bu was punished, and Jiawen was also sent out as prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huiqing took power, the earlier case was decided. Bu was punished and Jiawen was posted out as prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，安石復相，召檢正中書戶房。

translations.literal: The next year Anshi returned as chief minister and summoned him as Reviewing Director in the Secretariat's Household Section.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Anshi returned to office and summoned Jiawen back as Reviewing Director in the Secretariat's Household Section.

sentences.zh: 安石罷，以知江寧府。

translations.literal: When Anshi was dismissed, [Jiawen] was made prefect of Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi fell from power, he was appointed prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉運使何琬劾嘉問營繕越法，徙潤州，復坐免。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Transport Commissioner He Wan impeached Jiawen for unauthorized construction works; he was transferred to Runzhou and again punished and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Transport Commissioner He Wan impeached Jiawen for illegal construction. He was transferred to Runzhou and again dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，入為吏部郎中、光祿卿。

translations.literal: After a long while he entered the capital as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Director of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he returned to court as a director in the Ministry of Personnel and Director of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 言者交論市易之患，被於天下。

translations.literal: Speakers repeatedly debated the harm of the Market Exchange, which spread across all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Critics everywhere denounced the evils of the Market Exchange, which had spread across the empire.

sentences.zh: 本錢無慮千二百萬緡，率二分其息，十有五年之間，子本當數倍，今乃僅足本錢。

translations.literal: The principal capital was no less than twelve million strings; interest was generally two percent; over fifteen years principal and interest should have multiplied several times — yet now it barely equals the principal.
translations.idiomatic: The principal amounted to some twelve million strings at two percent interest. Over fifteen years the returns should have multiplied several times over, yet the treasury barely recovered its capital.

sentences.zh: 蓋買物入官，未轉售而先計息取賞；

translations.literal: This was because goods bought into government stores had interest calculated and rewards taken before they were resold;
translations.idiomatic: Officials recorded profits and claimed rewards before reselling goods the state had purchased;

sentences.zh: 至於物貨苦惡，上下相蒙，虧折日多，空有虛名而已。

translations.literal: as for goods they were wretched and inferior, superiors and subordinates deceived one another, losses mounted daily, and there was only an empty name.
translations.idiomatic: the merchandise was shoddy, superiors and subordinates colluded in fraud, losses mounted daily, and the enterprise existed in name alone.

sentences.zh: 於是削嘉問三秩，黜知淮陽軍，悉罪前被賞者。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiawen was stripped of three ranks, demoted as prefect of Huaiyang Command, and all previously rewarded persons were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Jiawen was demoted three ranks and sent out as prefect of Huaiyang Command, and all who had earlier been rewarded were punished.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，擢寶文閣待制、戶部侍郎，加直學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: In Shaosheng he was elevated to Attendant Gentleman of the Hall for Treasuring Culture, Vice Minister of Revenue, additionally given Direct Academician, and made prefect of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaosheng he was elevated to Attendant Gentleman of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and Vice Minister of Revenue, given the rank of Direct Academician, and appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 專附章惇、蔡卞，多殺不辜，焚去案牘以滅口。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to following Zhang Dun and Cai Bian, killed many innocents, and burned case records to silence evidence.
translations.idiomatic: He attached himself to Zhang Dun and Cai Bian, executed many innocent people, and burned court records to destroy the evidence.

sentences.zh: 嘗薦鄒浩，浩南遷，坐罷知懷州。

translations.literal: He once recommended Zou Hao; when Hao was sent south into exile, [Jiawen] was punished and dismissed as prefect of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had once recommended Zou Hao. When Hao was banished to the south, Jiawen was dismissed and made prefect of Huaizhou in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 徽宗時，屢暴其宿惡，至分司南京，光州居住，郢州安置。

translations.literal: In Huizong's time his old evils were repeatedly exposed; he was reduced to nominal service in Nanjing, residence in Guangzhou, and resettlement in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huizong his past crimes were exposed again and again. He was reduced to nominal duty in Nanjing, confined to Guangzhou, then resettled in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 然為蔡氏所右，其婿劉逵、蹇序辰、其死友鄧洵武羽翼之，故不久輒起。

translations.literal: Yet he was protected by the Cai faction — his sons-in-law Liu Kui and Jian Xuchen and his late friend Deng Xunwu supported him — so before long he was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The Cai faction protected him, however, backed by his sons-in-law Liu Kui and Jian Xuchen and by his late friend Deng Xunwu, so he was soon restored to office.

sentences.zh: 以龍圖閣學士、太中大夫卒，年七十七，贈資政殿學士。

translations.literal: He died holding the posts of Academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and Grand Master of Palace Affairs, aged seventy-seven; posthumously granted Academician of the Hall of Exemplary Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-seven while holding the ranks of Academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and Grand Master of Palace Affairs, and was posthumously granted Academician of the Hall of Exemplary Governance.

sentences.zh: 初，嘉問竊從祖公弼論新法奏稿，以示王安石，公弼以是斥於外，呂氏號為「家賊」，故不得與呂氏同傳。

translations.literal: At first Jiawen secretly took his grand-uncle Gongbi's memorial draft on the New Policies and showed it to Wang Anshi; Gongbi was for this expelled to the outside; the Lü clan called him "family traitor," and so he could not share a biographical record with the Lü clan.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Jiawen had stolen a draft memorial on the New Policies written by his grand-uncle Gongbi and shown it to Wang Anshi. Gongbi was driven from office for it, and the Lü clan branded Jiawen a "traitor in the family." For that reason he is not grouped with the other Lüs in this record.

sentences.zh: 李南公

translations.literal: Li Nangong
translations.idiomatic: Li Nangong

sentences.zh: 李南公，字楚老，鄭州人。

translations.literal: Li Nangong, styled Chulao, was a native of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nangong, styled Chulao, was a native of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，調浦江令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as magistrate of Pujiang.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he was appointed magistrate of Pujiang.

sentences.zh: 郡猾吏恃守以陵縣，不輸負租，南公捕繫之。

translations.literal: A cunning clerk of the prefecture relied on the prefect to bully the county and would not pay back rent owed; Nangong arrested and bound him.
translations.idiomatic: A cunning clerk in the prefecture, shielded by the prefect, bullied the county and refused to pay rent he owed. Nangong had him arrested.

sentences.zh: 守怒，通判為謝曰：「能按郡吏，健令也。

translations.literal: The prefect was angry; the vice-prefect apologized on his behalf, saying: "One who can prosecute a prefectural clerk is a vigorous magistrate."
translations.idiomatic: The prefect was furious. The vice-prefect apologized and said, "Any magistrate bold enough to prosecute a prefectural clerk is a forceful one."

sentences.zh: 」卒置諸法。

translations.literal: In the end [Nangong] applied the law to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Nangong had the law enforced against him.

sentences.zh: 知長沙縣，有嫠婦攜兒以嫁，七年，兒族取兒，婦謂非前子，訟於官。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Changsha County, there was a widow who brought her son in remarriage; after seven years the child's clan took the boy; the woman said he was not her former son and sued at court.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Changsha he heard a case in which a widow had remarried bringing her son with her. After seven years the boy's paternal clan reclaimed him. The woman claimed he was not her child by her first husband and sued.

sentences.zh: 南公問兒年，族曰九歲，婦曰七歲。

translations.literal: Nangong asked the boy's age; the clan said nine years, the woman said seven.
translations.idiomatic: Nangong asked the boy's age. The clan said nine; the woman said seven.

sentences.zh: 問其齒，曰：「去年毀矣。

translations.literal: He asked about his teeth and was told: "They fell out last year."
translations.idiomatic: He asked about the boy's teeth. "They came out last year," came the answer.

sentences.zh: 」南公曰：「男八歲而齔，尚何爭？

translations.literal: Nangong said: "A boy has his adult teeth at eight — what is there still to dispute?"
translations.idiomatic: Nangong said, "A boy gets his permanent teeth at eight. What is there left to dispute?"

sentences.zh: 」命歸兒族。

translations.literal: He ordered the boy returned to the clan.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the boy returned to his father's clan.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，提舉京西常平、提點陝西河北刑獄、京西轉運副使，入為屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: In the Xining era he served as Commissar of Western Capital Granaries, Judicial Intendant of Shaanxi and Hebei, and Vice Transport Commissioner of Western Capital Circuit, then entered the capital as Vice Director of the Directorate of Farming.
translations.idiomatic: During Xining he served as Commissar of Western Capital Granaries, Judicial Intendant for Shaanxi and Hebei, and Vice Transport Commissioner of the Western Capital Circuit, then entered court as Vice Director of the Directorate of Farming.

sentences.zh: 南公有女皆適人，而同產女弟年三十不嫁，寄他妹家，為御史所論，罷主管崇福宮。

translations.literal: Nangong's daughters had all married, but a younger sister by the same mother, aged thirty, had not married and lodged at another sister's home; censors impeached this and he was dismissed from supervising Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: All Nangong's daughters were married, but an unmarried younger sister of thirty was living with another sister. Censors impeached him over it and he was dismissed from his post supervising Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 為河北轉運副使。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Transport Commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Transport Commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 先是，知澶州王令圖請開迎陽埽舊河，於孫村置約回水東注，南公與范子奇以為可行，且欲於大吳北進鋸牙約河勢歸故道。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Lingtu, prefect of Dazhou, requested opening the old river at Yingyang Embankment, placing a weir at Suncun to turn water back east; Nangong and Fan Ziqi considered it feasible and also wished to advance saw-tooth weirs north of Dawu to compel the river's force back to its old course.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Lingtu, prefect of Dazhou, had proposed reopening the old channel at Yingyang Embankment and building a control works at Suncun to turn the current east again. Nangong and Fan Ziqi endorsed the plan and also proposed advancing saw-tooth weirs north of Dawu to drive the river back into its old bed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命使者行視，兩人復以前議為非，云：「迎陽下瞰京師，孫村水勢不便。

translations.literal: The court ordered emissaries to inspect on site; the two men again took their earlier proposal as wrong, saying: "Yingyang overlooks the capital from below; the water force at Suncun is inconvenient."
translations.idiomatic: When the court sent inspectors, the two reversed themselves and declared their earlier plan unsound, saying, "Yingyang lies below the capital, and the currents at Suncun would be dangerous."

sentences.zh: 」又為御史所論，詔罰金。

translations.literal: They were again impeached by censors and an edict fined them.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached them again, and an edict imposed fines.

sentences.zh: 加直秘閣、知延安府。

translations.literal: He was given Direct access to the Secret Archive and made prefect of Yan'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted Direct access to the Secret Archive and appointed prefect of Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 夏人犯涇原，南公出師搗其虛，夏人解去。

translations.literal: The Tangut invaded Jingyuan; Nangong marched out to strike their rear while undefended, and the Tangut withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut raided Jingyuan, Nangong led a force against their undefended rear and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進直龍閣閣，擢寶文閣待制、知瀛州，拜戶部吏部侍郎、戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Direct access to the Dragon Hall, elevated to Attendant Gentleman of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and prefect of Yingzhou, and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, Vice Minister of Personnel, and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted Direct access to the Dragon Hall, elevated to Attendant Gentleman of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and prefect of Yingzhou, and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, Vice Minister of Personnel, and Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 歷知永興軍、成都、真定、河南府、鄭州，擢龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Yongxing Command, Chengdu, Zhengding, Henan Prefecture, and Zhengzhou, and was elevated to Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Yongxing Command, Chengdu, Zhengding, Henan Prefecture, and Zhengzhou, and was elevated to Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs.

sentences.zh: 初，哲宗主入廟，南公修奉，希執政指，請祔東夾室，禮官爭之不得。

translations.literal: At first when Emperor Zhezong's tablet entered the ancestral temple, Nangong managed the rites, currying favor with the chief ministers, and requested enshrinement in the eastern side chamber; ritual officials disputed this but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong's tablet was first placed in the ancestral temple, Nangong oversaw the rites and, seeking favor with the chief ministers, proposed enshrining him in the eastern side chamber. Ritual officials objected in vain.

sentences.zh: 及更建廟室，坐前議弗當，奪學士，未幾，復之，遂致仕。

translations.literal: When the temple chambers were rebuilt, he was punished for his earlier improper proposal, stripped of academician rank; before long it was restored, and he then retired.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple was rebuilt he was punished for his earlier improper proposal and stripped of his academicianship. The rank was soon restored, after which he retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 南公為吏六十年，幹局明銳，然反覆詭隨，無特操，識者非之。

translations.literal: Nangong served as official for sixty years, with keen and sharp administrative capacity, yet he was reversal-prone, slippery, and without fixed principle; those who knew him disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Nangong served in office for sixty years. He was an able and sharp administrator, but he was erratic, opportunistic, and without fixed principles, and knowledgeable observers censured him for it.

sentences.zh: 子譓。

translations.literal: His son was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hui.

sentences.zh: 子 譓

translations.literal: Hui
translations.idiomatic: Hui

sentences.zh: 譓，字智甫。

translations.literal: Hui, styled Zhifu.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, styled Zhifu.

sentences.zh: 第進士。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 紹聖間，知章丘縣。

translations.literal: During Shaosheng he served as magistrate of Zhangqiu County.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaosheng he served as magistrate of Zhangqiu County.

sentences.zh: 陝西麥熟，朝廷議遣官諸州，令民平償逋負，譓與余景在選中。

translations.literal: When Shaanxi's wheat ripened, the court discussed sending officials to the various prefectures to have the people evenly repay arrears; Hui and Yu Jing were among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: When the wheat harvest came in Shaanxi, the court considered sending officials to each prefecture to collect overdue debts from the people. Hui and Yu Jing were among those chosen.

sentences.zh: 將賜對，曾布言於哲宗曰：「豐凶未可知，譓、景皆刻薄，必因此暴斂，為民之憂。

translations.literal: About to receive audience, Zeng Bu said to Zhezong: "Abundance or famine is not yet known; Hui and Jing are both harsh — they will surely use this to levy exactions and become the people's worry."
translations.idiomatic: Before their audience Zeng Bu told Zhezong, "We cannot yet know whether the harvest will be good or bad. Hui and Jing are both harsh men who will surely use this mission to extort the people."

sentences.zh: 陛下臨政以來，延見人士未多，如兩人者，懼不足以辱大對。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty began governing, you have extended audience to men of talent but not many; men like these two, I fear, are not worthy to defile a grand audience.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has granted audience to few men since taking the throne. Men like these are hardly fit for so solemn an occasion.

sentences.zh: 」乃喻使戒飭。

translations.literal: They were therefore instructed and admonished before departure.
translations.idiomatic: They were instructed accordingly and warned to behave.

sentences.zh: 使還，為河東轉運判官，徙陝西。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he served as Transport Assessor of Hedong and was transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After the mission he became Transport Assessor of Hedong and was then transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 進築京師，訖役，除秘閣校理。

translations.literal: He advanced [works on] fortifying the capital; when the project was finished he was appointed Collator in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw fortification work in the capital, and when the project was complete he was appointed Collator in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去。

translations.literal: He left office upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 方建永泰陵，起使京西。

translations.literal: Just as Yongtai Mausoleum was being built, he was recalled to serve in the Western Capital Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: While Yongtai Mausoleum was under construction, he was recalled to serve in the Western Capital Circuit.

sentences.zh: 諫官任伯雨言：「祖宗之世，朝廷有大事，邊鄙有兵革，將相大臣召為侍從，乃不得已奪情。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Ren Boyu said: "In the era of the ancestors, when the court had great affairs or the borderlands had warfare, generals, ministers, and great officers were summoned as attendants — only then was mourning obligation set aside as unavoidable."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Ren Boyu said, "Under the founding emperors, only when the court faced grave crises or the frontier erupted in war were great ministers summoned back to court and mourning set aside — and only when there was no choice."

sentences.zh: 今山陵事人 皆可辦，何至以一譓隳事體哉？

translations.literal: Now the mausoleum work can all be handled by people — why must one Hui ruin the propriety of the affair?
translations.idiomatic: The mausoleum work can be managed without him. Why should recalling one man like Hui compromise the dignity of the occasion?"

sentences.zh: 」命遂格。

translations.literal: The order was thereupon blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was cancelled.

sentences.zh: 終制，以直龍圖閣知熙州。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete he was made prefect of Xizhou with Direct access to the Hall of Dragon Designs.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning he was appointed prefect of Xizhou with Direct access to the Hall of Dragon Designs.

sentences.zh: 蔡京使王厚復河湟，譓與之異，召為光祿卿。

translations.literal: Cai Jing sent Wang Hou to recover the Hehuang region; Hui differed from him and was summoned as Director of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing sent Wang Hou to recover the Hehuang region, Hui opposed the plan and was recalled as Director of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 厚奏功，罷譓守虢。

translations.literal: Hou reported success; Hui was dismissed and made prefect of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou reported success, Hui was demoted to prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 坐嘗言招納未便，停官。

translations.literal: He was punished because he had once said that recruitment and pacification were inexpedient, and his office was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office for having once argued that the policy of recruiting and settling frontier peoples was ill-advised.

sentences.zh: 後數年，為陝西轉運使。

translations.literal: Several years later he served as Transport Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed Transport Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 京兆麥價踴貴，譓與府縣議從民和市，民弗肯損價。

translations.literal: In the Capital District wheat prices surged; Hui discussed with the prefecture and counties buying from the people at market prices, but the people would not reduce their prices.
translations.idiomatic: Wheat prices in the Capital District soared. Hui met with prefectural and county officials to arrange purchases from the people at market rates, but the sellers refused to lower their prices.

sentences.zh: 譓移府勒上戶閉糴，府帥徐處仁不聽，且責之。

translations.literal: Hui wrote to the prefecture ordering wealthy households to stop hoarding grain; the prefectural commander Xu Churen refused and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui wrote the prefecture demanding that wealthy households stop hoarding grain. The prefectural commander Xu Churen refused and reprimanded him.

sentences.zh: 譓怒，上章言處仁沮格詔令，陵毀使者。

translations.literal: Hui grew angry and memorialized that Churen obstructed imperial orders and insulted the emissary.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Hui submitted a memorial accusing Churen of blocking imperial orders and humiliating the imperial envoy.

sentences.zh: 詔黜處仁，而擢譓顯謨閣待制，代其任。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Churen and promoted Hui to Attendant Drafting Official in the Hall for Exalting Plans, replacing him in the post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed Churen from office and promoted Hui to Attendant Drafting Official in the Hall for Exalting Plans, appointing him in Churen's place.

sentences.zh: 鄜延帥錢昂奏：「處仁本以官糴麥損價，與譓爭，乃為民久長之論，不當黜。

translations.literal: Fuyan Military Commissioner Qian Ang memorialized: "Churen originally lowered the price of government-purchased wheat, arguing with Hui on behalf of the people's long-term welfare — he should not have been dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: Fuyan Military Commissioner Qian Ang memorialized, "Churen had lowered the price of government wheat purchases, disputing with Hui on grounds of the people's lasting welfare. He should not have been removed."

sentences.zh: 」詔以昂違道干譽，謫永州。

translations.literal: An edict punished Ang for violating the Way and seeking reputation, demoting him to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict condemned Ang for defying proper conduct to win praise and exiled him to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 譓又代任鄜延，復徙永興。

translations.literal: Hui again assumed the Fuyan post and was then transferred to Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Hui again took up the Fuyan command, then was transferred to Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 偽為蟾芝以獻，徽宗疑曰：「蟾，動物也，安得生芝？

translations.literal: He fabricated a toad fungus to present as tribute; Huizong questioned, saying: "The toad is a living creature — how could fungus grow from it?"
translations.idiomatic: He forged an auspicious "toad fungus" and presented it as tribute. Huizong was skeptical: "A toad is a living animal — how could fungus sprout from it?"

sentences.zh: 」命漬盆水，一夕而解。

translations.literal: He ordered it soaked in a basin of water; overnight it dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong had it soaked in a basin of water, and overnight it dissolved completely.

sentences.zh: 坐罔上，貶散官安置，三年復之。

translations.literal: Found guilty of deceiving the emperor, he was demoted to unsalaried official status under residence assignment; after three years he was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of deceiving the throne, he was stripped to unsalaried rank and placed under residence restriction. After three years his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 歷數郡，卒。

translations.literal: He served several prefectures and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served in several prefectures and then died.

sentences.zh: 董必，字子強，宣州南陵人。

translations.literal: Dong Bi, styled Ziqiang, was a native of Nanling in Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Bi, courtesy name Ziqiang, came from Nanling in Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗謁王安石於金陵，諮質諸經疑義，為安石稱許。

translations.literal: He once visited Wang Anshi in Jinling, consulting him on doubtful points in the classics, and was praised by Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: He once called on Wang Anshi in Jinling to consult him on obscure passages in the classics and won Anshi's praise.

sentences.zh: 登進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，提舉湖南常平。

translations.literal: During Shaosheng he served as Intendant of the Changping Granaries in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng era he served as Intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 時相章惇方置眾君子於罪。

translations.literal: At the time Chancellor Zhang Dun was placing numerous worthy men under accusation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chancellor Zhang Dun was finding fault with many upright officials.

sentences.zh: 孔平仲在衡州，以倉粟腐惡，乘饑歲，稍損價發之。

translations.literal: Kong Pingzhong was in Hengzhou; because the stored grain had spoiled, during a famine year he slightly reduced the price and released it.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Pingzhong was serving in Hengzhou. Finding the stored grain spoiled, he slightly reduced the price and released it during a famine year.

sentences.zh: 必即劾其戾常平法，置鞫長沙，以承惇意，無辜繫訊多死者。

translations.literal: Bi immediately impeached him for violating the Ever-Normal Granary law, set up interrogation in Changsha to comply with Dun's intentions — many innocents were detained and interrogated, and many died.
translations.idiomatic: Bi immediately impeached him for violating the Ever-Normal Granary law and set up an inquisition in Changsha to satisfy Dun. Many innocent people were imprisoned and interrogated, and many died.

sentences.zh: 平仲坐徙韶州。

translations.literal: Pingzhong was punished by transfer to Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong was punished with exile to Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 惇與蔡卞將大誅流人，遣呂升卿往廣東，必往廣西察訪。

translations.literal: Dun and Cai Bian planned a great purge of exiles, sending Lü Shengqing to Guangdong and Bi to Guangxi to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Dun and Cai Bian planned a sweeping purge of exiled officials, dispatching Lü Shengqing to Guangdong and Bi to Guangxi to investigate.

sentences.zh: 哲宗既止不治，然必所至，猶以慘刻按脅立威，為五書歸奏。

translations.literal: Although Zhezong had already ordered that no further action be taken, wherever Bi went he still used cruel severity to extort and establish authority, submitting five memorials on his return.
translations.idiomatic: Although Zhezong had already called a halt to further prosecutions, wherever Bi went he still used brutal coercion to assert his authority, and on returning submitted five memorials.

sentences.zh: 除工部員外郎，中書舍人郭知章封還其命；

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; Remonstrance Secretary Guo Zhizhang returned the appointment sealed.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works, but Remonstrance Secretary Guo Zhizhang sealed and returned the appointment.

sentences.zh: 詔以付趙挺之，權給事中陳次升復封駁不下。

translations.literal: An edict transferred the matter to Zhao Tingzhi; Acting Chief Drafting Secretary Chen Cisheng again sealed and rejected it, refusing to issue it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the appointment to Zhao Tingzhi, but Acting Chief Drafting Secretary Chen Cisheng again sealed and rejected it, refusing to promulgate it.

sentences.zh: 必於是訟知章、次升為元祐黨人。

translations.literal: Bi thereupon prosecuted Zhizhang and Cisheng as Yuanyou faction members.
translations.idiomatic: Bi then brought charges against Zhizhang and Cisheng as members of the Yuanyou faction.

sentences.zh: 坐不當訟言者，出知江州，改湖南轉運判官、提點河北刑獄，召為左司員外郎。

translations.literal: Punished for improperly prosecuting remonstrance officials, he was sent out as prefect of Jiangzhou, then changed to Transport Assessor of Hunan and Judicial Intendant of Hebei, and was summoned as Vice Director in the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for improperly prosecuting remonstrance officials, he was sent out as prefect of Jiangzhou, then served as Transport Assessor of Hunan and Judicial Intendant of Hebei before being recalled as Vice Director in the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，舒亶守荊南，起邊事，一切詐誕，云徭人款附，實亦不然，必蓋與之謀。

translations.literal: Initially, when Shu Dan guarded Jingnan, he stirred up border affairs — everything was fraudulent and absurd, claiming the Yao people had submitted when in fact they had not; Bi had likely conspired with him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shu Dan held Jingnan, he provoked border troubles with wholly fabricated claims that the Yao had submitted — which they had not. Bi had likely been his accomplice.

sentences.zh: 及是，亶暴卒，加必直龍圖閣往代。

translations.literal: At this time Dan died suddenly; Bi was given Direct access to the Hall of Dragon Designs and sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan died suddenly, Bi was granted Direct access to the Hall of Dragon Designs and sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 乃城通道等六砦，置靖州折博市易，且移飛山營戍。

translations.literal: He fortified six stockades including Tongdao, established a Jingzhou Barter and Market Exchange, and relocated the Feishan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He walled six stockades including Tongdao, established a Jingzhou barter exchange, and relocated the Feishan garrison.

sentences.zh: 公私煩費，荊人病之。

translations.literal: Public and private expenses became burdensome; the people of Jing were distressed.
translations.idiomatic: The costs burdened both public and private purses, and the people of Jingnan suffered.

sentences.zh: 進集賢殿修撰、顯謨閣待制。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Attendant Drafting Official in the Hall for Exalting Plans.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Attendant Drafting Official in the Hall for Exalting Plans.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十六，贈龍圖閣待制。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-six; posthumously awarded Attendant Drafting Official in the Hall of Dragon Designs.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-six and was posthumously granted the title Attendant Drafting Official in the Hall of Dragon Designs.

sentences.zh: 虞策，字經臣，杭州錢塘人。

translations.literal: Yu Ce, styled Jingchen, was a native of Qiantang in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ce, courtesy name Jingchen, came from Qiantang in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，調台州推官、知烏程縣、通判蘄州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed judicial adjutant in Taizhou, magistrate of Wucheng County, and vice-prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he served as judicial adjutant in Taizhou, magistrate of Wucheng County, and vice-prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 蔣之奇以江淮發運上計，神宗訪東南人才，以策對。

translations.literal: When Jiang Zhiqi came to court on grain transport business from the Jiang-Huai region, Shenzong inquired about southeastern talent and was answered with Ce.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Zhiqi came to court to present the Jiang-Huai transport accounts, Shenzong asked about talent in the southeast, and Jiang recommended Ce.

sentences.zh: 王安禮、李常繼薦之，擢提舉利州路常平、湖南轉運判官。

translations.literal: Wang Anli and Li Chang subsequently recommended him; he was promoted to Intendant of Changping in Lizhou Circuit and Transport Assessor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anli and Li Chang then recommended him, and he was promoted to Intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries in Lizhou Circuit and Transport Assessor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 元祐五年，召為監察御史，進右正言。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanyou he was summoned as Investigating Censor and advanced to Right Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanyou he was summoned as Investigating Censor and promoted to Right Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 數上書論事，謂人主納諫乃有福，治道以清靜為本。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs of state, saying that a ruler who accepts remonstrance will have fortune, and that the way of governance takes quiet simplicity as its foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted many memorials on affairs of state, arguing that a ruler who heeds remonstrance will prosper, and that good governance rests on quiet restraint.

sentences.zh: 西夏未順命，策言：「今邊備解弛，戎備不修。

translations.literal: When Western Xia had not yet submitted, Ce said: "Now frontier defenses are slack and military preparations neglected."
translations.idiomatic: When Western Xia had not yet submitted, Ce said, "Our frontier defenses are lax and our military readiness neglected."

sentences.zh: 古之人，善鎮靜者警備甚密，務持重者謀在其中，未有鹵莽闊疏，而曰吾鎮靜、吾持重者。

translations.literal: Men of antiquity who were skilled at remaining calm kept their vigilance extremely tight and placed their deliberations within a posture of weighty restraint — there never was one who was reckless and careless yet claimed 'I am calm' or 'I am restrained.'
translations.idiomatic: Men of old who mastered composure kept their guard extremely tight and buried their plans within a bearing of grave restraint. No one was ever reckless and slipshod yet claimed, 'I am calm' or 'I am restrained.'

sentences.zh: 」又乞詔內而省曹、寺監，外而監司、守令，各得以其職陳朝政闕失、百姓疾苦。

translations.literal: He also petitioned that edicts be issued so that within the court the ministry bureaus and directorates, and outside the circuit intendants and prefects, could each in their office set forth failures of court governance and the hardships of the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned for edicts allowing ministry bureaus and directorates within the court, and circuit intendants and local officials without, each to report in their proper capacity on failures of governance and the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 星文有變，乞順天愛民，警戒萬事，思治心修身之道，勿以宴安為樂。

translations.literal: When celestial signs changed, he petitioned to conform to Heaven and love the people, to be vigilant in all matters, to reflect on the ways of ordering the heart and cultivating the self, and not to take ease and comfort as pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: When celestial signs changed, he urged the emperor to follow Heaven's will and cherish the people, to be vigilant in all things, to reflect on how to order the heart and cultivate the self, and not to take comfort and idleness for joy.

sentences.zh: 哲宗納后，上《正始要言》。

translations.literal: When Zhezong took an empress, he submitted "Essential Words on the Beginning of Right Rule."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong took an empress, Ce submitted his "Essential Words on the Beginning of Right Rule."

sentences.zh: 遷左司諫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Secretariat Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Remonstrance Official in the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 曾肇以議北郊事，與朝論不合，免禮部侍郎，為徐州。

translations.literal: Zeng Zhao, because his views on the Northern Suburban Sacrifice differed from court opinion, was removed as Vice Minister of Rites and made prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Zhao, whose views on the Northern Suburban Sacrifice clashed with court opinion, was removed as Vice Minister of Rites and made prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 策時權給事中，還其命，以為肇禮官也，不當以議禮得罪。

translations.literal: Ce, then Acting Chief Drafting Secretary, returned the appointment, reasoning that Zhao was a ritual official and should not be punished for discussing ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Ce, then Acting Chief Drafting Secretary, returned the appointment, arguing that as a ritual official Zhao should not be punished merely for debating ritual matters.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 帝親政，條所當先者五十六事，後多施行。

translations.literal: When the emperor took personal rule, Ce listed fifty-six priorities; many were later implemented.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor began to rule in person, Ce listed fifty-six priorities; many were later adopted.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史、起居郎、給事中，以龍圖閣待制知青州，改杭州。

translations.literal: He was transferred through Attending Censor, Diarist, and Chief Drafting Secretary, then made prefect of Qingzhou as Attendant Drafting Official in the Hall of Dragon Designs, and changed to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Attending Censor, Diarist, and Chief Drafting Secretary, then served as prefect of Qingzhou as Attendant Drafting Official in the Hall of Dragon Designs before being transferred to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 過闕，留為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Passing the capital, he was retained as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through the capital on his way to a new post, he was kept on as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部、戶部尚書，拜樞密直學士，知永興軍、成都府。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Justice and Minister of Revenue, was appointed Privy Council Academician, and governed Yongxing Army and Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of Justice and Minister of Revenue, was appointed Privy Council Academician, and governed Yongxing Army and Chengdu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部尚書，奏疏徽宗，請均節財用，曰：「臣比在戶部，見中都經費歲六百萬，與天下上供之數略相當。

translations.literal: He entered court as Minister of Personnel, memorialized Huizong requesting balanced fiscal restraint, saying: "When I was in the Ministry of Revenue, I saw that the capital's annual expenditures were six million, roughly equal to the total tribute submitted from the entire empire."
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Minister of Personnel and memorialized Huizong urging balanced fiscal restraint: "When I served in the Ministry of Revenue, I found the capital's annual expenditures at six million — roughly equal to all tribute collected empire-wide."

sentences.zh: 嘗以祖宗故實考之，皇祐所入總三千九百萬，而費才三之一；
